1	# Unit Schema
2	
3	A "unit" is an atomic, AI-executable dev prompt derived from a (bound-)vault. Each unit corresponds to one bolt — one PR-sized code commit. Units are the contract handed off to `execute-bolts` via superpowers.
4	
5	## Contents
6	- Required frontmatter
7	- Required body sections (polished AI-coding-prompt shape)
8	- Hard rule grammar (closed 5-type set; EBNF + validation table)
9	- Per-task_type contracts
10	- Atomicity rules
11	- Multi-squad rules
12	- Interface reference resolution
13	- Dependency graph
14	- ID stability
15	- Greenfield vs brownfield (+ scope fields)
16	- Anti-hallucination rails
17	
18	(Note: the headings inside "Required body sections" — Goal, Context, Anchors, Hard rules, Anti-patterns, Implementation steps, Migration notes, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope — are the unit body's own section template, not sections of this reference.)
19	
20	## Required frontmatter
21	
22	```yaml
23	---
24	id: U-001                         # zero-padded, monotonic
25	title: <short imperative phrase>
26	vault_source: <doc>.md#<anchor>    # ONE grammar (v8 P0): <doc> = vault.md | model.md | flows.md |
27	                                   #   constraints.md | constitution.md (legacy 0N-*.md tolerated on read);
28	                                   #   <anchor> = the F-*/D-NNN id, the DBML table name, or the H2/H3
29	                                   #   heading slug the unit derives from (e.g. flows.md#F-U-001,
30	                                   #   model.md#contact_messages, vault.md#Architecture).
31	                                   # Readers are anchor-agnostic (SIT/UAT extract the F-id by search;
32	                                   # graph/emit key on `binding.json` claims, a DIFFERENT field with
33	                                   # its own `<doc>.md:<line>` grammar). Older shapes — `doc:anchor`,
34	                                   # `doc §anchor`, bare `doc` — are read-tolerated but reported by
35	                                   # validate-unit-spec.sh in the state's `vault_source_advisory`
36	                                   # (never a halt). New units: canonical form only.
37	task_type: create                  # create | extend | verify
38	                                   # create: new code, target_files all `create`
39	                                   # extend: modify existing; Migration notes mandatory
40	                                   #   AUTO-emitted for PARTIAL_FIELDS_* binding states with Migration notes populated from binding's field_diff
41	                                   # verify: NO code generation; only acceptance_test against existing implementation
42	                                   # Default: create. Auto-assigned from binding.md Implementation State Map when present.
43	status: implemented                # OPTIONAL (living-vault lifecycle; absence = legacy/not-yet-executed)
44	                                   # implemented: bolt committed AND all bolt-report target_hashes still match the working tree
45	                                   # stale: bolt committed BUT a target file changed since (per scripts/compute-unit-staleness.sh)
46	                                   #   - eligible for re-execution in the sync lane
47	                                   # superseded: the claim this unit derives from vanished from the (re-)bound vault
48	                                   #   - assigned ONLY by generate-units --reconcile; unit kept (audit trail), never deleted;
49	                                   #     execute-bolts SKIPS superseded units with a warning
50	grounding_confidence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW
51	risk: low | medium | high | critical   # OPTIONAL — written by generate-units Step 2.5 from the risk signals in references/adversarial-test-prompt.md (auth/payment/PII/regulatory-touching targets, LOCKED-claim refs); consumed by Step 9.5 (risk: high|critical auto-escalates to a separate adversarial-review subagent; critical bumps the review model). Absent = low.   # — reflects defensive generation checks
52	                                   # HIGH = binding present + all anchors verified + no target collisions + binding state all HIGH-conf
53	                                   #   AND (verify units only, A1) every acceptance criterion grounded in a NON-TEST source
54	                                   #   anchor `[grounded: path:line]` — see ## Acceptance criteria. A verify unit certifies
55	                                   #   EXISTING behavior; a criterion present only in a test stub / the PRD is NOT grounding.
56	                                   #   Any ungrounded criterion → NOT HIGH (downgrade, or split verify[built]+create[unbuilt]).
57	                                   #   Enforced: validate-unit-spec.sh halt verify_grounding_untrusted (HIGH verify units only).
58	                                   # MEDIUM = binding present BUT some anchors aspirational OR some UNKNOWN state OR codebase-map precision: regex
59	                                   # LOW = no binding (standalone generate-units) OR no codebase-map OR significant unverified anchors
60	                                   # Required on newly generated units; may be absent on legacy units.
61	mutability: "LOCKED — BI Reg 23/2/2021 §4: field name+type+validation MUST preserve (kb_locked)"
62	                                   # ONE QUOTED line: `<TIER> — <rationale incl. source>`, TIER = LOCKED | INTENT | ARTIFACT.
63	                                   # Quoting is MANDATORY — an unquoted rationale carrying a colon-space would
64	                                   # parse as a nested mapping and break the YAML frontmatter (repo authoring
65	                                   # standard). Absent → downstream treats as INTENT (safe default). The
66	                                   # ENFORCEABLE half of the old rebuild_freedom sub-map lives in `## Hard rules`
67	                                   # (DO_NOT_MODIFY / SIGNATURE productions) — unchanged. Legacy nested-map
68	                                   # units are tolerated — no reader parses this key.
69	squad: <squad-id>                  # OPTIONAL — required when ≥2 squads declared in _meta/squads.yaml
70	                                   # Format: squad-<kebab-case>. Omit or set to `default` for single-squad projects.
71	scope: <scope-id>                  # OPTIONAL — written when source vault.json has `scope` field
72	                                   # e.g., "BE", "MW", "FE". Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.id`.
73	                                   # Omitted entirely for legacy single-scope vaults.
74	scope_name: "<scope-name>"         # OPTIONAL — written alongside `scope:`
75	                                   # e.g., "Backend API". Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.name`.
76	                                   # Omitted entirely for legacy single-scope vaults.
77	reuse_candidates:                  # OPTIONAL — fast-path hints from reuse-index.yaml (NOT exhaustive; the bolt reads the full index)
78	  - { name: <symbol>, path: <file>, signature: <sig>, purpose: <1-line> }
79	                                   # Absent when no candidate matched; never fabricated.
80	                                   # These are hints — the bolt receives the full reuse-index.yaml path and scans it at write time.
81	module: <module-id>                # — semantic grouping per _meta/modules.yaml
82	                                   # Format: M-<kebab-case>. Auto-derived from vault_source matching modules.yaml.
83	                                   # M-default for vaults without modules.yaml. M-unassigned for unit's vault_source not matching any module.
84	depends_on: []                     # list of unit IDs that must complete first
85	                                   # MUST be same-squad units only when multi-squad mode active.
86	                                   # Cross-squad coupling MUST route through `consumes_interfaces` (see below).
87	target_files:                      # exact files this unit MAY touch (whitelist)
88	                                   # For task_type=verify: may be empty OR all entries `operation: none`
89	  - path: src/api/auth.ts
90	    operation: modify              # create | modify | delete | none (none for verify-type)
91	  - path: tests/auth.test.ts
92	    operation: create
93	existing_interfaces:               # contracts that MUST be preserved (in-codebase interfaces)
94	  - file: src/types/user.ts
95	    symbol: User
96	    note: "do not change shape; add optional field if needed"
97	produces_interfaces: []            # OPTIONAL — list of vault interface IDs this unit produces
98	                                   # Refs the kebab-id from interfaces/<id>.md frontmatter.
99	                                   # Only meaningful in multi-squad mode.
100	consumes_interfaces: []            # OPTIONAL — list of vault interface IDs this unit depends on
101	                                   # `execute-bolts` halts (cross_squad_interface_draft) if any referenced
102	                                   # interface has status: draft.
103	allowed_new_deps: []               # OPTIONAL (v5 P9) — the ALLOWLIST of new third-party
104	                                   # dependencies this unit sanctions. execute-bolts code gate 6
105	                                   # (the `validate-new-deps.sh --unit=` authorization concern) flags any dep the bolt ADDED that is
106	                                   # NOT in this list as `dep_unauthorized` (anti-over-engineering /
107	                                   # scope-creep, the WAJIB "pas" bar) — a deterministic ADVISORY finding
108	                                   # fed to the panel, never a halt. `[]` = "no new deps sanctioned".
109	                                   # ABSENT (v4/pre-v5 units) → the gate is a no-op (enforced:false), never
110	                                   # a finding. Distinct from the `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS` Hard rule (which BLOCKS
111	                                   # ALL new deps via B1); this is the graduated, advisory allowlist form.
112	acceptance_test:                   # how to verify the bolt succeeded
113	  - type: test                     # test | manual | lint | typecheck | render
114	    command: "npm test -- auth"
115	    expects: ""                    # SUBSTRING MATCHER, not a description: run-acceptance-tests.sh
116	                                   # passes an entry when exit==0 AND (expects is EMPTY OR expects
117	                                   # appears LITERALLY in the runner's output). Fill it ONLY with a
118	                                   # literal string the runner actually prints (e.g. jest prints
119	                                   # "passed", never "passes"); when you cannot cite one, LEAVE IT
120	                                   # EMPTY — exit code 0 is the criterion. A description here makes
121	                                   # every run fail (field defect: 4 units needed fix commits because
122	                                   # this very example used to be the description-shaped poison).
123	    ears: "WHEN a login request carries an expired token THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 401 with problem+json"
124	                                   # OPTIONAL (additive, backward-compatible) — an EARS-shaped statement
125	                                   # ("WHEN <trigger> THE SYSTEM SHALL <response>" / "WHILE <state> ..." /
126	                                   # "IF <condition> THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL ...") making the criterion
127	                                   # machine-checkable. Emit ONLY when the EARS statement adds behavioral
128	                                   # precision absent from `expects:` (e.g. expects is empty);
129	                                   # NEVER a restatement of expects — nothing parses ears downstream.
130	                                   # When present the bolt's TDD test MUST assert exactly this statement
131	                                   # (and PBT properties MAY be derived from it).
132	                                   # Absent → `expects:` (a literal output substring, or empty =
133	                                   # exit-code criterion) remains the criterion (no behavior change);
134	                                   # validators tolerate absence everywhere.
135	  - type: manual
136	    desc: "Hit /login with valid creds, expect 200 + token"
137	  - type: render                   # REQUIRED for any unit whose target_files include a
138	                                   # detail/show view (code-delivery slice D). Asserts the
139	                                   # detail route renders a real field — catches empty-model
140	                                   # show / branch `—` / null-timestamp crashes a route-200
141	                                   # smoke test misses. Derived from the active framework
142	                                   # pack `## Test patterns` -> detail_view_render template.
143	    command: "php artisan test --filter WidgetShowRendersTest"
144	    expects: ""                    # same substring contract — the render REQUIREMENT (route 200 +
145	                                   # real display field asserted) lives in the TEST's own assertions,
146	                                   # never as prose in expects
147	prd_source: docs/PRD.md#halaman-kontak   # v8 P1 (spec 2026-09-10 App. F1) — the PRD heading (`<prd-file>#<heading-slug>`,
148	                                   #   slug = lowercase, non-alphanumerics → `-`) or line (`<prd-file>:<line>`) this
149	                                   #   unit implements; repo-relative; a YAML list is allowed. RESOLVED by
150	                                   #   validate-unit-spec.sh when present (halt prd_source_unresolvable — a citation
151	                                   #   to a heading that does not exist is a fabricated requirement); absent =
152	                                   #   legacy unit, tolerated. Input of validate-plan-coverage.sh (P1.d).
153	context_source: flows.md#F-U-001   # v8 P1 — alias of vault_source (same `<doc>.md#<anchor>` grammar); writers
154	                                   #   emit ONE of the two (v7 chain: vault_source; v8 PLAN: context_source).
155	binding_refs:                      # binding manifest IDs this unit honors
156	  - C-001
157	  - OQ-012
158	---
159	```
160	
161	**Legacy keys.** Pre-diet units may carry `grounding_evidence` / `superpowers_skills` / `estimated_complexity` / a nested `mutability` map — readers tolerate all of them; `generate-units` no longer writes them. **v8 P1 writer diet (spec App. F1d):** the consumer census 2026-09-10 found ZERO readers for `mutability`, `estimated_complexity`, `grounding_evidence`, `superpowers_skills` and `acceptance_test[].ears` — new units MUST NOT carry them. The diet is writer-side only: no validator requires their absence.
162	
163	## Required body sections (polished AI-coding-prompt shape)
164	
165	**xs body diet (v8 P1, spec 2026-09-10 App. F1e).** A unit with 1–2 `acceptance_test` entries AND 1–3 implementation steps is the router's `unit_tier: xs` class (`scripts/_lib/unit_tier.py` — the ONE size proxy shared by `resolve-review-tier.sh` and `validate-unit-spec.sh`). Its body is embedded verbatim in every dispatch prompt, so for that class: **Goal = 1 line · Context ≤ 2 sentences · Implementation steps ≤ 3 · `## Anti-patterns` and `## Out of scope` only when every item cites a source** (U-XXX, OQ-, C-, doc anchor, file:line). `validate-unit-spec.sh` records offenders in the state's `xs_body_advisory` list (advisory — never an issue, status or halt). Non-xs units keep the shape below.
166	
167	```markdown
168	## Goal
169	<1-2 sentences — what this unit produces; xs class: ONE line>
170	
171	## Context (read first)
172	<which vault sections, which binding entries, KB sections (if KB present), and WHY this scope exists. Conversational directive prose, NOT bullets. Aim for 2-4 sentences that orient an AI coding agent (xs class: ≤ 2): what's the surrounding system, what's the user-visible outcome, what changes nothing.>
173	
174	## Anchors  (mandatory for ALL task_types when binding evidence exists)
175	<file:line where existing code lives that this unit references or modifies. AI coding agent reads these BEFORE writing.>
176	<For task_type=verify and task_type=extend: MANDATORY — cite the implementation anchor from binding.>
177	<For task_type=create: MANDATORY when at least one binding entry exists pointing to a related pattern in codebase-map. Cite the closest pattern to follow. Optional when fully greenfield.>
178	
179	- src/Http/Controllers/UserController.php:45-67 — existing pattern; follow this shape
180	- src/Models/User.php:12 — entity to extend
181	- .mega-sdd/knowledge-base/modules/customer.prd.md §2 (if KB present; legacy numbered tree: docs/knowledge-base/10-domains/<domain>.md §5) — domain behavior to honor
182	
183	## Claims  (v8 P1 — brownfield units only; a CONTRACT about existing code, never a verdict)
184	<One line per expectation about EXISTING code this unit relies on or changes. Verdicts are NEVER written here — the JIT bind at dispatch (execute-bolts pre-flight 3.9, spec App. F2–F4) verifies each line and records CONFIRMED/CONFLICT/OQ in the hook-guarded `bolts/U-XXX/binding.json`. Greenfield / create-only units omit the section (their claims derive from target_files: create ⇒ must-not-exist).>
185	
186	- C-U005-01 "Nasabah model has field `nip` (unique)" — expect: app/Models/Nasabah.php:Nasabah
187	- C-U005-02 "no login route exists yet" — expect: routes/web.php — must-not-exist
188	- C-U005-03 "migration for nasabah table exists" — expect: database/migrations — must-exist
189	
190	Grammar: `- C-U<NNN>-<NN> "<verbatim expectation>" — expect: <path>[:<symbol>] | <path> — must-exist | <path> — must-not-exist`. `<path>[:<symbol>]` ⇒ symbol claim (symbol index); bare `<path>` with must-exist/must-not-exist ⇒ filesystem claim (0 model tokens); a quoted expectation without a resolvable symbol ⇒ text claim (ladder E3, express-bind.md).
191	
192	## Hard rules  (validated at bolt time by execute-bolts pre/post-flight)
193	<Machine-parseable constraints. Grammar closed in v1 per DESIGN-OQ-4 (5 rule types). One rule per line. Empty section allowed (no rules to enforce).>
194	
195	- DO NOT modify <path>
196	- DO NOT add new <manifest-file> dependencies
197	- file:<path-glob> MUST follow <case-style> naming
198	- function <name> MUST preserve signature: <type-signature>
199	- file <path> MUST exist after bolt
200	
201	## Anti-patterns  (guidance, NOT validated)
202	<Conversational don'ts drawn from binding CONFLICTS + KB gotchas + tech-OQ recommendations + experience. AI agent reads these as context; not machine-enforced. xs class: omit the section unless every item cites its source.>
203	
204	- Don't bypass middleware `auth.role` — RBAC pattern in routes/web.php:34
205	- Don't replicate the typo `cfkdhl → CFKDDL` from legacy at <legacy-anchor>
206	- Don't add a new HTTP error envelope; existing pattern at ErrorResource.php:12 is canonical
207	
208	## Implementation steps  (directive prose, not bullet schema)
209	<Written like a senior teammate briefing another teammate. AT LEAST one sentence >15 words. Reference Anchors inline. Avoid pure bullet checklists.>
210	<For task_type=verify: ONE line — "No code changes. Run acceptance tests against existing implementation at <anchor>.">
211	<For task_type=create: directive prose explaining the build sequence with anchor references.>
212	<For task_type=extend: directive prose with explicit "first read Anchor A to see existing shape; then add X following that shape" framing.>
213	
214	First, open `app/Http/Controllers/UserController.php` and look at the `index` method at line 45 to see how the existing read endpoints structure their response. Then add a `store` method that mirrors this shape but accepts validated input from `StoreUserRequest`. The trickier part is the role assignment — see the Anchor at `routes/api.php:34` for how roles are attached after the existing flow.
215	
216	## Migration notes  (mandatory for task_type=extend; omitted otherwise)
217	<Three sub-lists when this section is present:>
218	- **REMOVE**: <code to delete>
219	- **KEEP**: <code to preserve, do not touch>
220	- **ADD**: <new code to write>
221	
222	## Acceptance criteria
223	<Written ONCE — the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries are the structured authority; this section is per-task_type.>
224	<For task_type=create|extend: the section body is ONE pointer line — "Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter
225	 `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative)." — plus ONLY lines that add information the structured entries
226	 cannot carry: TBD OQ items ("TBD: <OQ-ID> — <question>") and prose-only constraints. NEVER a verbatim
227	 expansion of each entry's command/expects.>
228	<For task_type=verify: expanded criteria at ALL confidence levels (marker-bearing when grounding_confidence
229	 is HIGH) — a verify unit always keeps its expanded body criteria; the A1 grounding substrate lives here.
230	 ALL acceptance criteria must assert behavior of existing implementation — not new behavior.>
231	<For task_type=verify with grounding_confidence: HIGH (A1 — per-AC source grounding): prefix EACH criterion
232	 with a grounding marker that proves the asserted behavior already exists in NON-TEST source:
233	   - [grounded: src/Services/Purchase.php:142] the 4th daily purchase is rejected
234	   - [grounded: app/config/limits.php:8] minimum purchase is enforced at Rp 10.000
235	 A criterion you cannot ground — its behavior lives only in a test stub, the PRD, or nowhere yet — is marked
236	   - [ungrounded] source-of-fund validation
237	 and means the unit is NOT verify+HIGH: downgrade grounding_confidence, OR split a verify[built] unit (the
238	 grounded criteria) from a create[unbuilt] unit (the ungrounded ones). A test-file path is NOT grounding
239	 (tests can assert behavior that does not exist). Once ANY criterion carries a marker the unit opts in and
240	 EVERY criterion must be `[grounded: <non-test path>:<line>]`; legacy units with no markers are tolerated.
241	 Enforced by validate-unit-spec.sh → verify_grounding_untrusted (blocks the next execute-bolts).>
242	
243	## Out of scope (for this unit)
244	<explicit list — prevents scope creep into adjacent units. xs class: omit unless every item names where it lives (U-XXX / OQ-)>
245	```
246	
247	## Hard rule grammar (closed v1)
248	
249	Five mechanical rule types + a directive tier (generic `MUST/MUST NOT/DO NOT/NEVER/ALWAYS` prose — accepted but not machine-checkable; recorded `attested` with `--attest-directives` else `directive_unverified` at post-flight). Modal-synonym carve-out: `MUST NOT modify <path>` / `NEVER add new <manifest> dependencies` with a PATH-SHAPED object (contains `.` or `/`) classify as the mechanical productions, never directive — they cannot be attested past; a prose object (`MUST NOT modify existing API contracts`) stays a directive. A line matching neither a mechanical type nor the directive tier → halt at bolt time with `hard_rule_unparseable`.
250	
251	```ebnf
252	RULE := DO_NOT_MODIFY | DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS | NAMING_RULE | SIGNATURE_RULE | FILE_PRESENCE_RULE
253	
254	DO_NOT_MODIFY        := "DO NOT modify " <path>
255	DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS      := "DO NOT add new " <manifest> " dependencies"
256	NAMING_RULE          := <path-glob> " MUST follow " <case-style> " naming"
257	SIGNATURE_RULE       := "function " <name> " MUST preserve signature: " <type-sig>
258	FILE_PRESENCE_RULE   := "file " <path> " MUST exist after bolt"
259	
260	where:
261	  <path>          = relative or absolute file path
262	  <path-glob>     = glob pattern (file:src/api/*.ts)
263	  <manifest>      = package.json | composer.json | Cargo.toml | go.mod | etc.
264	  <case-style>    = kebab-case | camelCase | snake_case | PascalCase
265	  <name>          = identifier (function name)
266	  <type-sig>      = parenthesized parameter list with types + return type
267	```
268	
269	### Examples
270	
271	```
272	DO NOT modify src/Models/User.php
273	DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
274	file:src/api/*.ts MUST follow kebab-case naming
275	function authenticateUser MUST preserve signature: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<User>
276	file src/Models/AuditLog.php MUST exist after bolt
277	```
278	
279	### Validation by execute-bolts
280	
281	| Rule type | Pre-flight check | Post-flight check |
282	|---|---|---|
283	| `DO_NOT_MODIFY` | Snapshot file checksum | Compare checksum; differs → violated |
284	| `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS` | Snapshot manifest content | Diff manifest; new top-level entry under deps/dependencies/etc. → violated |
285	| `NAMING_RULE` | (none — new-file only) | Apply case-style regex against all new files matching glob; mismatch → violated |
286	| `SIGNATURE_RULE` | Snapshot function signature via codebase-map symbol lookup | Re-extract signature; differs → violated |
287	| `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE` | (none) | Probe path exists in repo; missing → violated |
288	
289	A line matching neither a mechanical type nor the directive tier is unparseable → halt with `hard_rule_unparseable` blocker. NEVER silently skip.
290	
291	### Per-task_type contracts
292	
293	| task_type | target_files | Anchors | Migration notes | acceptance_test | Implementation steps body |
294	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
295	| `create` | All `operation: create` | Optional (cite related patterns) | Omitted | Tests for new functionality | Numbered build steps |
296	| `extend` | At least one `operation: modify`; new files allowed `operation: create` | MANDATORY | MANDATORY (REMOVE/KEEP/ADD) | Tests for new behavior; existing-behavior assertions in `existing_interfaces` | Numbered modification steps |
297	| `verify` | Empty OR all `operation: none` | MANDATORY (cite the existing implementation) | Omitted | All assertions against existing implementation | ONE line: "No code changes. Run acceptance tests against existing implementation at <anchor>." |
298	
299	> `generate-units` auto-emits `create` and `verify` types based on the binding's Implementation State Map.
300	>
301	> `extend` type is AUTO-EMITTED when bind-codebase detects `PARTIAL_FIELDS_MISSING` / `PARTIAL_FIELDS_SURPLUS` / `PARTIAL_FIELDS_BOTH` states. Migration notes populated from binding's `field_diff` column (ADD/KEEP/REMOVE lists). User can override via interactive prompt for PARTIAL_FIELDS_SURPLUS (which signals ambiguity between feature drift / vault gap / legacy / rename).
302	
303	## Atomicity rules
304	
305	- One unit = one PR-sized commit. If the body steps would produce >300 lines of code change, SPLIT into multiple sequential units (allocated U-00N at Step 6 topological numbering) with an explicit `depends_on` chain — never dotted sub-IDs (U-001.1 would break the content-hash ID-stability contract `--refresh`/`--reconcile` depend on). The >300 LOC / ≤5 files threshold is an authoring judgment (advisory — no validator measures it). Under granularity `large` (`--max-complexity=large` / config `unit_granularity: coarse`, 7.20.0) the threshold rises to >600 LOC / ≤8 files — same advisory class, "PR-sized" becomes "story-sized"; every other rail (whitelist, task_type, Hard rules, per-unit review) is granularity-independent.
306	- `target_files` whitelist is enforced by `execute-bolts` at three layers: the dispatch prompt forbids out-of-whitelist writes (rules tier), the review panel checks scope (judgment tier), and the deterministic B3 whitelist observer (`validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --whitelist-scan`, Stop-hook + gate-time) diffs each bolted unit's COMMITTED paths against `target_files` ∪ sanctioned extras (vault/bolt artifacts, `.mega-sdd/`, test files) — escaped paths block the next `execute-bolts` with `whitelist_violation`.
307	- `existing_interfaces` is enforced by acceptance tests — any test against a listed interface must continue passing.
308	- `task_type` is enforced by `execute-bolts` — `verify` units MUST NOT modify any file; violations are halt-conditions at bolt time.
309	- `## Hard rules` body section is parsed at bolt time. Pre-flight snapshots state; post-flight validates against the implementer's landed commit (detect-after topology per execute-bolts SKILL.md). Violations halt with `hard_rule_violated` and gate further bolts until fixed.
310	- `## Implementation steps` MUST contain at least one sentence >15 words (directive prose check). Pure bullet checklists trigger render-pass warning.
311	
312	## Multi-squad rules
313	
314	Applies only when `_meta/squads.yaml` exists with ≥2 squads. Single-squad / no-squad-config vaults skip these rules.
315	
316	- `squad:` field is REQUIRED on every unit. `generate-units` assigns based on the routing rules in `generate-intent/references/squad-partition.md` (cross-skill ref — the layer-hint table, hybrid feature>layer priority, and squads.yaml validation live there).
317	- `depends_on` MUST reference units with the SAME `squad:`. Cross-squad direct deps are rejected with `cross_squad_dep_invalid` halt.
318	- Cross-squad coupling MUST go through interface notes:
319	  - Producer side: declare `produces_interfaces: [<id>, ...]` listing every interface this unit creates/implements.
320	  - Consumer side: declare `consumes_interfaces: [<id>, ...]` listing every interface this unit reads/calls.
321	- Every entry in `produces_interfaces` and `consumes_interfaces` MUST exist as an `interfaces/<id>.md` file in the vault. Dangling references fail validation.
322	- A unit that `consumes_interfaces` a `status: draft` interface CAN be generated but CANNOT be executed: `execute-bolts` halts with `cross_squad_interface_draft` until the producer squad locks the interface.
323	
324	## Interface reference resolution
325	
326	When `generate-units` emits a unit with `consumes_interfaces: [api-leave-request-submit]`:
327	1. Verify `<vault>/interfaces/api-leave-request-submit.md` exists.
328	2. Read its frontmatter: `producer`, `status`.
329	3. Confirm `producer` squad ≠ the unit's `squad` (it's a CROSS-squad interface, not intra-squad).
330	4. Record the interface's status — `execute-bolts` reads this at execution time to decide halt vs run.
331	
332	## Dependency graph
333	
334	`depends_on` builds a DAG. `generate-units` rejects cycles. `execute-bolts` topologically sorts the graph; independent units may run in parallel under `subagent-driven-development`.
335	
336	## ID stability
337	
338	Unit IDs are stable across regenerations:
339	- `diff-vault` preserves IDs by content hash
340	- `generate-units` with `--refresh` flag re-numbers; default does not
341	
342	## Greenfield vs brownfield
343	
344	- **Greenfield:** units derived directly from vault (no binding). `binding_refs` is empty.
345	- **Brownfield:** units derived from bound-vault. `binding_refs` populated; OQs propagate to unit acceptance criteria as "TBD: <question>" items.
346	
347	### Scope fields
348	
349	Optional fields written ONLY when source vault.json has `scope` field (multi-scope vault):
350	
351	- `scope: <id>` — e.g., `BE`, `MW`, `FE`. Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.id`.
352	- `scope_name: "<name>"` — e.g., `"Backend API"`. Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.name`.
353	
354	Omitted entirely for legacy single-scope vaults (no `scope` field in source vault.json).
355	
356	## Anti-hallucination rails
357	
358	- Unit MAY ONLY reference vault sections + binding entries (cited explicitly).
359	- Unit MAY ONLY touch files listed in `target_files`.
360	- Unit MUST have at least one acceptance_test entry of type `test`. No exceptions.
361	- (slice D) Any unit whose `target_files` include a detail/show view (matching the active framework pack `## Test patterns` -> `detail_view_glob`) MUST ALSO carry at least one acceptance_test entry of type `render`. Absent → `validate-unit-spec.sh` emits `render_test_missing` and BLOCKS `execute-bolts`. The render test is derived from the pack `detail_view_render` template; a prose `## Tests` / `## Acceptance` bullet does NOT satisfy this — it must be a structured `acceptance_test:` entry with `type: render` (or `kind: render`). Packs that omit `## Test patterns` → check SKIPs (the stack never declared a detail-view convention).
362	- If unit body cannot meet a contract, halt — do not generate a partial unit.
363	- In multi-squad mode, `depends_on` MUST be intra-squad only. Cross-squad direct deps halt with `cross_squad_dep_invalid`.
364	- `consumes_interfaces` entries MUST resolve to existing interface files; status field is read at bolt time to gate execution.
365	- `scope:` / `scope_name:` MUST be sourced verbatim from vault.json `scope_metadata`. NEVER inferred or invented. Omit both fields when vault has no `scope` field.
366

# Unit Schema

A "unit" is an atomic, AI-executable dev prompt derived from a (bound-)vault. Each unit corresponds to one bolt — one PR-sized code commit. Units are the contract handed off to `execute-bolts` via superpowers.

## Contents
- Required frontmatter
- Required body sections (polished AI-coding-prompt shape)
- Hard rule grammar (closed 5-type set; EBNF + validation table)
- Per-task_type contracts
- Atomicity rules
- Multi-squad rules
- Interface reference resolution
- Dependency graph
- ID stability
- Greenfield vs brownfield (+ scope fields)
- Anti-hallucination rails

(Note: the headings inside "Required body sections" — Goal, Context, Anchors, Hard rules, Anti-patterns, Implementation steps, Migration notes, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope — are the unit body's own section template, not sections of this reference.)

## Required frontmatter

```yaml
---
id: U-001                         # zero-padded, monotonic
title: <short imperative phrase>
vault_source: <doc>.md#<anchor>    # ONE grammar (v8 P0): <doc> = vault.md | model.md | flows.md |
                                   #   constraints.md | constitution.md (legacy 0N-*.md tolerated on read);
                                   #   <anchor> = the F-*/D-NNN id, the DBML table name, or the H2/H3
                                   #   heading slug the unit derives from (e.g. flows.md#F-U-001,
                                   #   model.md#contact_messages, vault.md#Architecture).
                                   # Readers are anchor-agnostic (SIT/UAT extract the F-id by search;
                                   # graph/emit key on `binding.json` claims, a DIFFERENT field with
                                   # its own `<doc>.md:<line>` grammar). Older shapes — `doc:anchor`,
                                   # `doc §anchor`, bare `doc` — are read-tolerated but reported by
                                   # validate-unit-spec.sh in the state's `vault_source_advisory`
                                   # (never a halt). New units: canonical form only.
task_type: create                  # create | extend | verify
                                   # create: new code, target_files all `create`
                                   # extend: modify existing; Migration notes mandatory
                                   #   AUTO-emitted for PARTIAL_FIELDS_* binding states with Migration notes populated from binding's field_diff
                                   # verify: NO code generation; only acceptance_test against existing implementation
                                   # Default: create. Auto-assigned from binding.md Implementation State Map when present.
status: implemented                # OPTIONAL (living-vault lifecycle; absence = legacy/not-yet-executed)
                                   # implemented: bolt committed AND all bolt-report target_hashes still match the working tree
                                   # stale: bolt committed BUT a target file changed since (per scripts/compute-unit-staleness.sh)
                                   #   - eligible for re-execution in the sync lane
                                   # superseded: the claim this unit derives from vanished from the (re-)bound vault
                                   #   - assigned ONLY by generate-units --reconcile; unit kept (audit trail), never deleted;
                                   #     execute-bolts SKIPS superseded units with a warning
grounding_confidence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW

## Hard rule grammar (closed v1)

Five mechanical rule types + a directive tier (generic `MUST/MUST NOT/DO NOT/NEVER/ALWAYS` prose — accepted but not machine-checkable; recorded `attested` with `--attest-directives` else `directive_unverified` at post-flight). Modal-synonym carve-out: `MUST NOT modify <path>` / `NEVER add new <manifest> dependencies` with a PATH-SHAPED object (contains `.` or `/`) classify as the mechanical productions, never directive — they cannot be attested past; a prose object (`MUST NOT modify existing API contracts`) stays a directive. A line matching neither a mechanical type nor the directive tier → halt at bolt time with `hard_rule_unparseable`.

```ebnf
RULE := DO_NOT_MODIFY | DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS | NAMING_RULE | SIGNATURE_RULE | FILE_PRESENCE_RULE

DO_NOT_MODIFY        := "DO NOT modify " <path>
DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS      := "DO NOT add new " <manifest> " dependencies"
NAMING_RULE          := <path-glob> " MUST follow " <case-style> " naming"
SIGNATURE_RULE       := "function " <name> " MUST preserve signature: " <type-sig>
FILE_PRESENCE_RULE   := "file " <path> " MUST exist after bolt"

where:
  <path>          = relative or absolute file path
  <path-glob>     = glob pattern (file:src/api/*.ts)
  <manifest>      = package.json | composer.json | Cargo.toml | go.mod | etc.
  <case-style>    = kebab-case | camelCase | snake_case | PascalCase
  <name>          = identifier (function name)
  <type-sig>      = parenthesized parameter list with types + return type
```

### Examples

```
DO NOT modify src/Models/User.php
DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
file:src/api/*.ts MUST follow kebab-case naming
function authenticateUser MUST preserve signature: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<User>
file src/Models/AuditLog.php MUST exist after bolt
```

### Validation by execute-bolts

| Rule type | Pre-flight check | Post-flight check |
|---|---|---|
| `DO_NOT_MODIFY` | Snapshot file checksum | Compare checksum; differs → violated |
| `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS` | Snapshot manifest content | Diff manifest; new top-level entry under deps/dependencies/etc. → violated |
| `NAMING_RULE` | (none — new-file only) | Apply case-style regex against all new files matching glob; mismatch → violated |
| `SIGNATURE_RULE` | Snapshot function signature via codebase-map symbol lookup | Re-extract signature; differs → violated |
| `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE` | (none) | Probe path exists in repo; missing → violated |

A line matching neither a mechanical type nor the directive tier is unparseable → halt with `hard_rule_unparseable` blocker. NEVER silently skip.

### Per-task_type contracts

| task_type | target_files | Anchors | Migration notes | acceptance_test | Implementation steps body |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | All `operation: create` | Optional (cite related patterns) | Omitted | Tests for new functionality | Numbered build steps |
| `extend` | At least one `operation: modify`; new files allowed `operation: create` | MANDATORY | MANDATORY (REMOVE/KEEP/ADD) | Tests for new behavior; existing-behavior assertions in `existing_interfaces` | Numbered modification steps |
| `verify` | Empty OR all `operation: none` | MANDATORY (cite the existing implementation) | Omitted | All assertions against existing implementation | ONE line: "No code changes. Run acceptance tests against existing implementation at <anchor>." |

> `generate-units` auto-emits `create` and `verify` types based on the binding's Implementation State Map.
>
> `extend` type is AUTO-EMITTED when bind-codebase detects `PARTIAL_FIELDS_MISSING` / `PARTIAL_FIELDS_SURPLUS` / `PARTIAL_FIELDS_BOTH` states. Migration notes populated from binding's `field_diff` column (ADD/KEEP/REMOVE lists). User can override via interactive prompt for PARTIAL_FIELDS_SURPLUS (which signals ambiguity between feature drift / vault gap / legacy / rename).

## Atomicity rules

- One unit = one PR-sized commit. If the body steps would produce >300 lines of code change, SPLIT into multiple sequential units (allocated U-00N at Step 6 topological numbering) with an explicit `depends_on` chain — never dotted sub-IDs (U-001.1 would break the content-hash ID-stability contract `--refresh`/`--reconcile` depend on). The >300 LOC / ≤5 files threshold is an authoring judgment (advisory — no validator measures it). Under granularity `large` (`--max-complexity=large` / config `unit_granularity: coarse`, 7.20.0) the threshold rises to >600 LOC / ≤8 files — same advisory class, "PR-sized" becomes "story-sized"; every other rail (whitelist, task_type, Hard rules, per-unit review) is granularity-independent.
- `target_files` whitelist is enforced by `execute-bolts` at three layers: the dispatch prompt forbids out-of-whitelist writes (rules tier), the review panel checks scope (judgment tier), and the deterministic B3 whitelist observer (`validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --whitelist-scan`, Stop-hook + gate-time) diffs each bolted unit's COMMITTED paths against `target_files` ∪ sanctioned extras (vault/bolt artifacts, `.mega-sdd/`, test files) — escaped paths block the next `execute-bolts` with `whitelist_violation`.
- `existing_interfaces` is enforced by acceptance tests — any test against a listed interface must continue passing.
- `task_type` is enforced by `execute-bolts` — `verify` units MUST NOT modify any file; violations are halt-conditions at bolt time.
- `## Hard rules` body section is parsed at bolt time. Pre-flight snapshots state; post-flight validates against the implementer's landed commit (detect-after topology per execute-bolts SKILL.md). Violations halt with `hard_rule_violated` and gate further bolts until fixed.
- `## Implementation steps` MUST contain at least one sentence >15 words (directive prose check). Pure bullet checklists trigger render-pass warning.

## Multi-squad rules

Applies only when `_meta/squads.yaml` exists with ≥2 squads. Single-squad / no-squad-config vaults skip these rules.

- `squad:` field is REQUIRED on every unit. `generate-units` assigns based on the routing rules in `generate-intent/references/squad-partition.md` (cross-skill ref — the layer-hint table, hybrid feature>layer priority, and squads.yaml validation live there).
- `depends_on` MUST reference units with the SAME `squad:`. Cross-squad direct deps are rejected with `cross_squad_dep_invalid` halt.
- Cross-squad coupling MUST go through interface notes:
  - Producer side: declare `produces_interfaces: [<id>, ...]` listing every interface this unit creates/implements.
  - Consumer side: declare `consumes_interfaces: [<id>, ...]` listing every interface this unit reads/calls.
- Every entry in `produces_interfaces` and `consumes_interfaces` MUST exist as an `interfaces/<id>.md` file in the vault. Dangling references fail validation.
- A unit that `consumes_interfaces` a `status: draft` interface CAN be generated but CANNOT be executed: `execute-bolts` halts with `cross_squad_interface_draft` until the producer squad locks the interface.

## Interface reference resolution

When `generate-units` emits a unit with `consumes_interfaces: [api-leave-request-submit]`:
1. Verify `<vault>/interfaces/api-leave-request-submit.md` exists.
2. Read its frontmatter: `producer`, `status`.
3. Confirm `producer` squad ≠ the unit's `squad` (it's a CROSS-squad interface, not intra-squad).
4. Record the interface's status — `execute-bolts` reads this at execution time to decide halt vs run.

## Dependency graph

`depends_on` builds a DAG. `generate-units` rejects cycles. `execute-bolts` topologically sorts the graph; independent units may run in parallel under `subagent-driven-development`.

## ID stability

Unit IDs are stable across regenerations:
- `diff-vault` preserves IDs by content hash
- `generate-units` with `--refresh` flag re-numbers; default does not

## Greenfield vs brownfield

- **Greenfield:** units derived directly from vault (no binding). `binding_refs` is empty.
- **Brownfield:** units derived from bound-vault. `binding_refs` populated; OQs propagate to unit acceptance criteria as "TBD: <question>" items.

### Scope fields

Optional fields written ONLY when source vault.json has `scope` field (multi-scope vault):

- `scope: <id>` — e.g., `BE`, `MW`, `FE`. Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.id`.
- `scope_name: "<name>"` — e.g., `"Backend API"`. Matches vault.json `scope_metadata.name`.

Omitted entirely for legacy single-scope vaults (no `scope` field in source vault.json).

## Anti-hallucination rails

- Unit MAY ONLY reference vault sections + binding entries (cited explicitly).
- Unit MAY ONLY touch files listed in `target_files`.
- Unit MUST have at least one acceptance_test entry of type `test`. No exceptions.
- (slice D) Any unit whose `target_files` include a detail/show view (matching the active framework pack `## Test patterns` -> `detail_view_glob`) MUST ALSO carry at least one acceptance_test entry of type `render`. Absent → `validate-unit-spec.sh` emits `render_test_missing` and BLOCKS `execute-bolts`. The render test is derived from the pack `detail_view_render` template; a prose `## Tests` / `## Acceptance` bullet does NOT satisfy this — it must be a structured `acceptance_test:` entry with `type: render` (or `kind: render`). Packs that omit `## Test patterns` → check SKIPs (the stack never declared a detail-view convention).
- If unit body cannot meet a contract, halt — do not generate a partial unit.
- In multi-squad mode, `depends_on` MUST be intra-squad only. Cross-squad direct deps halt with `cross_squad_dep_invalid`.
- `consumes_interfaces` entries MUST resolve to existing interface files; status field is read at bolt time to gate execution.
- `scope:` / `scope_name:` MUST be sourced verbatim from vault.json `scope_metadata`. NEVER inferred or invented. Omit both fields when vault has no `scope` field.

# Adversarial Acceptance-Test Review Prompt

> Prompt template for `generate-units` Step 9.5 — adversarial review of acceptance_test authored in Step 9. Closes audit Pattern F structural risk (D4-006): "Never trust AI to both generate and validate" (ACM FSE 2025).

**Consumed by:** `generate-units/SKILL.md` Step 9.5
**Output target:** updates `acceptance_test` in unit frontmatter with merged gap assertions + sets `_authored_by:` provenance field

## Contents
- Default mode (main-thread self-re-prompt)
- Opt-in subagent mode (`--adversarial-subagent`)
- Gap merge logic (Step 9.5 post-review)
- `_authored_by:` provenance values
- Anti-halu rails

---

## Default mode (main-thread self-re-prompt)

The main thread, after authoring the unit body + acceptance_test in Step 9, re-prompts itself with the following framing BEFORE writing the unit file. No subagent dispatch needed.

```
ROLE: QA engineer reviewing an acceptance_test for completeness.

UNIT (verbatim from Step 9):
<paste the just-generated unit body>

CURRENT acceptance_test (verbatim):
<paste the just-generated acceptance_test block>

YOUR JOB:
Find AT LEAST 2 cases where this acceptance_test would FAIL to catch a real
bug in the implementation. For each case:

- Describe the bug scenario (e.g., "what if user_id is null but the request
  still returns HTTP 200?")
- Identify which existing test assertion would miss it (e.g., "test only
  checks HTTP status code; never inspects response body shape")
- Propose the additional test assertion that would catch it (test code OR
  natural-language assertion the bolt subagent can translate)

Be ADVERSARIAL: assume the original test author had blind spots. The goal is
to find what they missed, NOT to validate what they wrote. If the test looks
"obviously fine" to you, look harder — that's a sign you're inheriting the
same blind spots.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT rewrite the entire acceptance_test. Only identify gaps and propose
  targeted additions.
- Do NOT propose gaps that are out-of-scope for this unit (e.g., suggesting
  load tests when the unit is about CRUD correctness). Per-unit scope matters.
- If the unit body is genuinely tight and the test covers it well, return
  `coverage_verdict: strong` + empty `gaps_identified`. Honest "no gaps
  found" is better than fabricated gaps.

OUTPUT FORMAT (strict YAML):
```yaml
adversarial_review:
  reviewer_pass: 2                          # always 2 (after Step 9 = pass 1)
  gaps_identified:
    - scenario: "<bug case description>"
      missed_by_assertion: "<which existing assertion fails to catch it>"
      proposed_additional_assertion: "<test code or natural language>"
    # repeat per gap; aim for AT LEAST 2 unless coverage_verdict is strong
  coverage_verdict: weak | adequate | strong
```
```

## Opt-in subagent mode (`--adversarial-subagent` flag)

When user passes `--adversarial-subagent` to `generate-units`, OR when unit frontmatter declares `risk: high`, dispatch a SEPARATE subagent for the adversarial review. Separate LLM context = stronger blind-spot coverage at the cost of one extra dispatch per high-risk unit.

> **Who writes `risk:`** — generate-units Step 2.5 stamps the frontmatter field when a unit's target_files/binding_refs hit the risk signals (auth/authn/authz surfaces, payment/money movement, PII/regulated data, `[LOCKED]`-claim refs, security-sensitive packs). Without the stamp, escalation only fires via the manual `--adversarial-subagent` flag.

Subagent dispatch contract:
- Model: sonnet (default; opus for `risk: critical` units)
- Tool surface: Read, Grep (read-only)
- Wall-clock budget: ≤3 min per unit
- Output format: same YAML structure as default mode

Subagent is dispatched per-unit; main thread iterates units sequentially when `--adversarial-subagent` is set (no parallel — keeps simplifikasi).

## Gap merge logic (generate-units Step 9.5 post-review)

Main thread (NOT the adversarial reviewer) handles merge:

1. If `coverage_verdict: strong` AND `gaps_identified: []` → keep original acceptance_test as-is; set `_authored_by: adversarial-reviewed (no gaps)`
2. If `gaps_identified: [...]` non-empty → for each gap, append `proposed_additional_assertion` to acceptance_test as new test case. Set `_authored_by: adversarial-reviewed (+N gaps merged)` where N = count
3. If `coverage_verdict: weak` AND `gaps_identified: []` (incoherent) → keep original acceptance_test; set `_authored_by: adversarial-review-failed (kept original; manual review recommended)`. Log warning to chat.

## `_authored_by:` provenance values (canonical)

| Value | Origin | Trust signal |
|---|---|---|
| `same-pass` | legacy unit (field absent) OR `--no-adversarial-review` flag set | weakest |
| `adversarial-reviewed` | default; gaps merged or no-gap finding | recommended baseline |
| `adversarial-reviewed (no gaps)` | adversarial pass found nothing to add | strong |
| `adversarial-reviewed (+N gaps merged)` | N gaps merged into test | strong |
| `adversarial-review-failed` | adversarial pass returned incoherent output | weak + warning |
| `independent-llm` | `--adversarial-subagent` flag, separate subagent extended test | strongest LLM |
| `human` | user manually edited acceptance_test post-generation | strongest overall |

Legacy units (no field present) → treat as `same-pass` for execute-bolts surface logic.

## Anti-halu rails

- Adversarial reviewer MUST NOT modify the unit body — only proposes test additions
- Adversarial reviewer MUST output strict YAML matching the schema above; parse failures → fallback to `same-pass` provenance + log warning
- `--no-adversarial-review` flag preserved for users who explicitly want the same-pass behavior (debug / regression testing)
- Legacy units re-encountered by `generate-units --regenerate` get the adversarial review pass on rewrite; user-marked `_authored_by: human` units are preserved untouched

1	# Modules Schema
2	
3	Semantic grouping layer ABOVE units. Units stay atomic (1 unit = 1 PR-sized commit invariant); modules aggregate related units per domain / flow / component for human mental-model fit + progress tracking + filtered execution.
4	
5	Per user UX request — units felt "too small" cognitively; need module-level grouping to match team mental model (auth phase, leave-mgmt phase, etc.).
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Why modules ≠ bigger units
9	- Vault layout addition
10	- `_meta/modules.yaml` schema
11	- Auto-derivation rules (when modules.yaml absent)
12	- Unit frontmatter extension
13	- `_index.md` template (grouped by module)
14	- Module dependency graph
15	- Module-level DoD validation
16	- Filtered execution (`execute-bolts --module=<id>`)
17	- Module-level progress in memory
18	- Halt protocol additions
19	- Backward compatibility
20	- Migration
21	- References
22	
23	## Why modules ≠ bigger units
24	
25	Module = **semantic grouping** (like Jira Epic over Stories). Units = **atomic implementation work** (TDD-discipline + bolt-focus + rollback granularity preserved). The two layer; neither replaces the other.
26	
27	| Concern | Larger atomic units | Modules over atomic units (THIS DESIGN) |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| TDD cycle | One test per huge unit — long cycle | One test per atomic unit — fast cycle |
30	| Hard Rule scoping | Muddled across surface | Clear per atomic boundary |
31	| Bolt focus | LLM context diluted | LLM holds one unit at a time |
32	| Git rollback granularity | Coarse | Per-unit |
33	| Parallelism (`--per-squad`, `--parallel`) | Lower | Preserved |
34	| Semantic grouping | "Sort of" via larger size | Explicit via module field |
35	| Progress tracking | Per-unit (overwhelming) | Per-module (meaningful) + per-unit (detail) |
36	
37	Modules are the strictly-better answer for the user's stated pain.
38	
39	## Vault layout addition
40	
41	```
42	<vault>/
43	├── vault.md
44	├── model.md / flows.md / constraints.md
45	├── vault.json
46	├── _meta/
47	│   ├── squads.yaml                  # multi-squad
48	│   └── modules.yaml                 # semantic grouping
49	├── units/
50	│   ├── U-*.md                       # each unit gains `module: <id>` frontmatter field
51	│   └── _index.md                    # grouped by module (NEW format)
52	└── (binding.md, bound/, bolts/, etc.)
53	```
54	
55	## `_meta/modules.yaml` schema
56	
57	```yaml
58	mega_sdd_schema: 1
59	modules:
60	  - id: <kebab-case identifier with M- prefix>     # e.g., M-auth, M-leave-mgmt, M-reporting
61	    name: <human-readable display name>             # e.g., "Authentication & Authorization"
62	    description: <1-2 sentences>                    # optional
63	    vault_sections:                                  # which vault sections this module covers
64	      - <vault-file>#<anchor>                       # e.g., flows.md#F-U-001-login
65	      - <vault-file>#<section-name>
66	    dod:                                             # Definition of Done (module-level)
67	      - <checklist item>                            # e.g., "All auth flows return RFC 7807 errors"
68	      - <test command>                              # e.g., "phpunit tests/Feature/Auth*.php passing"
69	    estimated_units: <range>                         # e.g., "5-8" — optional sizing hint
70	    priority: P0 | P1 | P2 | P3
71	    blocks: []                                       # module IDs that depend on this one
72	    blocked_by: []                                   # module IDs this one depends on
73	```
74	
75	## Auto-derivation rules (when modules.yaml absent)
76	
77	If user does NOT provide `_meta/modules.yaml`, `generate-units` auto-derives a minimal modules.yaml from vault structure:
78	
79	| Vault structure signal | Auto-derived module |
80	|---|---|
81	| Each `## F-U-*` section in `flows.md` (user flow) | One module per top-level user flow group |
82	| Each component in `vault.md ## Architecture` (named component) | One module per architectural component |
83	| Each `### D-*` ADR group in `vault.md ## Decisions` referencing same domain | Implicit grouping (advisory; doesn't generate module) |
84	
85	Auto-derivation produces a `_meta/modules.yaml.auto` file (note `.auto` suffix). User can rename to `modules.yaml` to lock in OR edit before re-running generate-units.
86	
87	## Unit frontmatter extension
88	
89	```yaml
90	---
91	id: U-007
92	title: Add nama field to login endpoint
93	module: M-auth                       # references _meta/modules.yaml
94	vault_source: flows.md#F-U-001-login
95	task_type: extend
96	grounding_confidence: HIGH
97	# ... existing fields ...
98	---
99	```
100	
101	### Module assignment algorithm in `generate-units`
102	
103	For each unit's `vault_source`, find matching module:
104	
105	```
106	for module in modules.yaml.modules:
107	  for section in module.vault_sections:
108	    if unit.vault_source matches section (file + anchor or section-name):
109	      unit.module = module.id
110	      break
111	  if unit.module is set: break
112	
113	if unit.module is still null:
114	  unit.module = "M-unassigned"   # fallback (no halt; surface warning in chat)
115	```
116	
117	`M-unassigned` is special — units not matching any module. Render warning: "N units have no module; consider adding vault section to modules.yaml or creating new module."
118	
119	## `_index.md` template (grouped by module)
120	
121	```markdown
122	# Vault Units Index
123	
124	**Total units**: N
125	**Modules**: M (5 modules — see _meta/modules.yaml)
126	
127	---
128	
129	## M-auth — Authentication & Authorization
130	**Status**: in-progress (2/5 complete)
131	**Priority**: P0
132	**DoD**:
133	- [ ] All auth flows return RFC 7807 errors
134	- [x] Sanctum middleware applied to /api/* routes
135	- [ ] phpunit tests/Feature/Auth*.php passing
136	
137	Units (dependency order):
138	| ID | Title | task_type | depends_on | status |
139	|---|---|---|---|---|
140	| U-001 | Create LoginController | create | (none) | ✓ done |
141	| U-002 | Add LoginRequest validator | create | U-001 | ✓ done |
142	| U-003 | Add Sanctum auth middleware | create | U-001 | pending |
143	| U-007 | Add nama field to login | extend | U-001, U-002 | pending |
144	| U-008 | Add password reset flow | create | U-001 | pending |
145	
146	---
147	
148	## M-leave-mgmt — Leave Management
149	**Status**: not-started (0/3 complete)
150	**Priority**: P1
151	**DoD**:
152	- [ ] End-to-end leave request UAT passes
153	- [ ] Approval chain matches RBAC config
154	
155	Units (dependency order):
156	| ID | Title | task_type | depends_on | status |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| U-010 | Create LeaveRequest model | create | (none) | pending |
159	| U-011 | Add /api/leave endpoints | create | U-010 | pending |
160	| U-012 | Add approval workflow | create | U-011 | pending |
161	
162	---
163	
164	## M-unassigned (1 unit — no module match)
165	
166	⚠️ Consider adding this unit's vault section to modules.yaml OR creating a new module.
167	
168	| ID | Title | vault_source |
169	|---|---|---|
170	| U-015 | Add audit log table | model.md#AuditLog |
171	```
172	
173	## Module dependency graph
174	
175	Modules can have `blocks` / `blocked_by` for inter-module ordering. Example:
176	
177	```yaml
178	- id: M-auth
179	  blocks: [M-leave-mgmt, M-reporting]  # other modules can't start until M-auth done
180	  blocked_by: []
181	
182	- id: M-leave-mgmt
183	  blocks: []
184	  blocked_by: [M-auth]                 # waits for M-auth
185	```
186	
187	`generate-units` validates: every unit's `depends_on` is consistent with its module's `blocked_by`. Cross-module unit dependencies require explicit module-level `blocked_by` declaration.
188	
189	## Module-level DoD validation
190	
191	The list-modules diagnostic (`orchestrate-flow/references/diagnostics-procedures.md §list-modules`, or the `execute-bolts --module=<id>` completion check) probes each DoD item:
192	
193	- Checklist items (Markdown `- [ ] / [x]`) → toggleable; user marks done
194	- Test commands → can be auto-run: detect command string; invoke via Bash; pass/fail logged to memory
195	- Module marked `completed` when ALL DoD items pass
196	
197	## Filtered execution (`execute-bolts --module=<id>`)
198	
199	```bash
200	execute-bolts --module=M-auth
201	```
202	
203	Runs only units where `module: M-auth`. Topologically sorted within module. Respects cross-module `blocked_by` declarations — halts with `module_blocked_by` blocker if dependencies not done.
204	
205	## Module-level progress in memory
206	
207	After each unit completes:
208	
209	- `<vault>/.memory/bolt-outcomes.json` already tracks per-unit outcomes (existing)
210	- Module progress derived: `units in module M-X where status=completed / total units in M-X`
211	- the list-modules diagnostic (`query-graph.sh --modules`) reads this for live progress display
212	
213	## Halt protocol additions
214	
215	| Halt type | When |
216	|---|---|
217	| `module_unassigned_warn` | ≥10% of units have `module: M-unassigned`. Warning (not blocking); halts only with `--strict-modules` flag |
218	| `module_blocked_by` | execute-bolts --module=X invoked but X.blocked_by has incomplete module Y |
219	| `module_dod_unsat` | module declared completed but DoD items still pending (user attempts to mark done prematurely) |
220	| `cross_module_dep_invalid` | unit's depends_on crosses module boundary AND that module isn't declared in blocked_by |
221	
222	## Backward compatibility
223	
224	- v3.4 vaults without `_meta/modules.yaml` → all units get `module: M-default` (single implicit module)
225	- v3.4 unit files without `module:` field → treated as M-default
226	- `_index.md` falls back to flat list (no grouping) when only M-default exists
227	- `execute-bolts --module=<id>` works for M-default-only vaults (just runs all units)
228	- Existing `vault_source` field is the primary signal for auto-derivation
229	
230	## Migration
231	
232	Existing v3.4 vaults can opt into modules by:
233	
234	1. Adding `_meta/modules.yaml` — manually, OR by promoting the auto-derivation output: any `generate-units` run's Step 4.5 writes `_meta/modules.yaml.auto`; review it, then `mv _meta/modules.yaml.auto _meta/modules.yaml` (execute-bolts' `--module=` halt accepts only the promoted name)
235	2. Re-running `generate-units --reconcile` — refreshes Step 5 module assignment against the existing unit set without regenerating unit bodies
236	3. Optional: edit `modules.yaml` to refine grouping; re-run `--reconcile`
237	
238	## References
239	
240	- The atomic unit definition (the unit-schema reference listed in the skill router) — unchanged by this layer
241	- `squads.yaml` — the social partition (orthogonal to modules)
242	- This file — the semantic grouping layer above atomic units
243	- `orchestrate-flow/references/diagnostics-procedures.md §list-modules` — module progress query procedure (relocated from `commands/list-modules.md` in the surface cull)

# Modules Schema

Semantic grouping layer ABOVE units. Units stay atomic (1 unit = 1 PR-sized commit invariant); modules aggregate related units per domain / flow / component for human mental-model fit + progress tracking + filtered execution.

Per user UX request — units felt "too small" cognitively; need module-level grouping to match team mental model (auth phase, leave-mgmt phase, etc.).

## Contents
- Why modules ≠ bigger units
- Vault layout addition
- `_meta/modules.yaml` schema
- Auto-derivation rules (when modules.yaml absent)
- Unit frontmatter extension
- `_index.md` template (grouped by module)
- Module dependency graph
- Module-level DoD validation
- Filtered execution (`execute-bolts --module=<id>`)
- Module-level progress in memory
- Halt protocol additions
- Backward compatibility
- Migration
- References

## Why modules ≠ bigger units

Module = **semantic grouping** (like Jira Epic over Stories). Units = **atomic implementation work** (TDD-discipline + bolt-focus + rollback granularity preserved). The two layer; neither replaces the other.

| Concern | Larger atomic units | Modules over atomic units (THIS DESIGN) |
|---|---|---|
| TDD cycle | One test per huge unit — long cycle | One test per atomic unit — fast cycle |
| Hard Rule scoping | Muddled across surface | Clear per atomic boundary |
| Bolt focus | LLM context diluted | LLM holds one unit at a time |
| Git rollback granularity | Coarse | Per-unit |
| Parallelism (`--per-squad`, `--parallel`) | Lower | Preserved |
| Semantic grouping | "Sort of" via larger size | Explicit via module field |
| Progress tracking | Per-unit (overwhelming) | Per-module (meaningful) + per-unit (detail) |

Modules are the strictly-better answer for the user's stated pain.

## Vault layout addition

```
<vault>/
├── vault.md
├── model.md / flows.md / constraints.md
├── vault.json
├── _meta/
│   ├── squads.yaml                  # multi-squad
│   └── modules.yaml                 # semantic grouping
├── units/
│   ├── U-*.md                       # each unit gains `module: <id>` frontmatter field
│   └── _index.md                    # grouped by module (NEW format)
└── (binding.md, bound/, bolts/, etc.)
```

## `_meta/modules.yaml` schema

```yaml
mega_sdd_schema: 1
modules:
  - id: <kebab-case identifier with M- prefix>     # e.g., M-auth, M-leave-mgmt, M-reporting
    name: <human-readable display name>             # e.g., "Authentication & Authorization"
    description: <1-2 sentences>                    # optional
    vault_sections:                                  # which vault sections this module covers
      - <vault-file>#<anchor>                       # e.g., flows.md#F-U-001-login
      - <vault-file>#<section-name>
    dod:                                             # Definition of Done (module-level)
      - <checklist item>                            # e.g., "All auth flows return RFC 7807 errors"
      - <test command>                              # e.g., "phpunit tests/Feature/Auth*.php passing"
    estimated_units: <range>                         # e.g., "5-8" — optional sizing hint
    priority: P0 | P1 | P2 | P3
    blocks: []                                       # module IDs that depend on this one
    blocked_by: []                                   # module IDs this one depends on
```

## Auto-derivation rules (when modules.yaml absent)

If user does NOT provide `_meta/modules.yaml`, `generate-units` auto-derives a minimal modules.yaml from vault structure:

| Vault structure signal | Auto-derived module |
|---|---|
| Each `## F-U-*` section in `flows.md` (user flow) | One module per top-level user flow group |
| Each component in `vault.md ## Architecture` (named component) | One module per architectural component |
| Each `### D-*` ADR group in `vault.md ## Decisions` referencing same domain | Implicit grouping (advisory; doesn't generate module) |

Auto-derivation produces a `_meta/modules.yaml.auto` file (note `.auto` suffix). User can rename to `modules.yaml` to lock in OR edit before re-running generate-units.

## Unit frontmatter extension

```yaml
---
id: U-007
title: Add nama field to login endpoint
module: M-auth                       # references _meta/modules.yaml
vault_source: flows.md#F-U-001-login
task_type: extend
grounding_confidence: HIGH
# ... existing fields ...
---
```

### Module assignment algorithm in `generate-units`

For each unit's `vault_source`, find matching module:

```
for module in modules.yaml.modules:
  for section in module.vault_sections:
    if unit.vault_source matches section (file + anchor or section-name):
      unit.module = module.id
      break
  if unit.module is set: break

if unit.module is still null:
  unit.module = "M-unassigned"   # fallback (no halt; surface warning in chat)
```

`M-unassigned` is special — units not matching any module. Render warning: "N units have no module; consider adding vault section to modules.yaml or creating new module."

## `_index.md` template (grouped by module)

```markdown
# Vault Units Index

**Total units**: N
**Modules**: M (5 modules — see _meta/modules.yaml)

---

## M-auth — Authentication & Authorization
**Status**: in-progress (2/5 complete)

- [x] Sanctum middleware applied to /api/* routes

Units (dependency order):

| U-001 | Create LoginController | create | (none) | ✓ done |
| U-002 | Add LoginRequest validator | create | U-001 | ✓ done |
| U-003 | Add Sanctum auth middleware | create | U-001 | pending |
| U-007 | Add nama field to login | extend | U-001, U-002 | pending |
| U-008 | Add password reset flow | create | U-001 | pending |

---

## M-leave-mgmt — Leave Management
**Status**: not-started (0/3 complete)
**Priority**: P1
**DoD**:

- [ ] Approval chain matches RBAC config

Units (dependency order):

---

## M-unassigned (1 unit — no module match)

⚠️ Consider adding this unit's vault section to modules.yaml OR creating a new module.

| ID | Title | vault_source |
|---|---|---|
| U-015 | Add audit log table | model.md#AuditLog |
```

## Module dependency graph

Modules can have `blocks` / `blocked_by` for inter-module ordering. Example:

```yaml
- id: M-auth
  blocks: [M-leave-mgmt, M-reporting]  # other modules can't start until M-auth done
  blocked_by: []

- id: M-leave-mgmt
  blocks: []
  blocked_by: [M-auth]                 # waits for M-auth
```

`generate-units` validates: every unit's `depends_on` is consistent with its module's `blocked_by`. Cross-module unit dependencies require explicit module-level `blocked_by` declaration.

## Module-level DoD validation

The list-modules diagnostic (`orchestrate-flow/references/diagnostics-procedures.md §list-modules`, or the `execute-bolts --module=<id>` completion check) probes each DoD item:

- Checklist items (Markdown `- [ ] / [x]`) → toggleable; user marks done
- Test commands → can be auto-run: detect command string; invoke via Bash; pass/fail logged to memory
- Module marked `completed` when ALL DoD items pass

## Filtered execution (`execute-bolts --module=<id>`)

```bash
execute-bolts --module=M-auth
```

Runs only units where `module: M-auth`. Topologically sorted within module. Respects cross-module `blocked_by` declarations — halts with `module_blocked_by` blocker if dependencies not done.

## Module-level progress in memory

After each unit completes:

- `<vault>/.memory/bolt-outcomes.json` already tracks per-unit outcomes (existing)
- Module progress derived: `units in module M-X where status=completed / total units in M-X`
- the list-modules diagnostic (`query-graph.sh --modules`) reads this for live progress display

## Halt protocol additions

| Halt type | When |
|---|---|
| `module_unassigned_warn` | ≥10% of units have `module: M-unassigned`. Warning (not blocking); halts only with `--strict-modules` flag |
| `module_blocked_by` | execute-bolts --module=X invoked but X.blocked_by has incomplete module Y |
| `module_dod_unsat` | module declared completed but DoD items still pending (user attempts to mark done prematurely) |
| `cross_module_dep_invalid` | unit's depends_on crosses module boundary AND that module isn't declared in blocked_by |

## Backward compatibility

- v3.4 vaults without `_meta/modules.yaml` → all units get `module: M-default` (single implicit module)
- v3.4 unit files without `module:` field → treated as M-default
- `_index.md` falls back to flat list (no grouping) when only M-default exists
- `execute-bolts --module=<id>` works for M-default-only vaults (just runs all units)
- Existing `vault_source` field is the primary signal for auto-derivation

## Migration

Existing v3.4 vaults can opt into modules by:

1. Adding `_meta/modules.yaml` — manually, OR by promoting the auto-derivation output: any `generate-units` run's Step 4.5 writes `_meta/modules.yaml.auto`; review it, then `mv _meta/modules.yaml.auto _meta/modules.yaml` (execute-bolts' `--module=` halt accepts only the promoted name)
2. Re-running `generate-units --reconcile` — refreshes Step 5 module assignment against the existing unit set without regenerating unit bodies
3. Optional: edit `modules.yaml` to refine grouping; re-run `--reconcile`

## References

- The atomic unit definition (the unit-schema reference listed in the skill router) — unchanged by this layer
- `squads.yaml` — the social partition (orthogonal to modules)
- This file — the semantic grouping layer above atomic units
- `orchestrate-flow/references/diagnostics-procedures.md §list-modules` — module progress query procedure (relocated from `commands/list-modules.md` in the surface cull)

# Propose-and-Confirm Prompt Template

## One-screen halt (W1 zero-idle, v8 P1.e — spec 2026-09-10 App. F6d)

A BLOCKING halt (`binding_conflict`/`bind_conflict`, `hard_rule_violated`, OQ P1 business — the only three that may wait for a human mid-run) is rendered as ONE screen with exactly three parts, in this order, nothing else above the options: (1) **Apa yang berhenti** — one line: unit id, halt type, the offending claim/rule/OQ verbatim (≤ 2 lines of evidence with `file:line`); (2) **Satu pertanyaan** — the single decision the human must make, phrased so a non-engineer can answer (keterangan contract, `references/output-language.md §OQ authoring`); (3) **Opsi** — the AskUserQuestion options for that halt (CONFLICT: KEEP_VAULT / KEEP_CODE / SPLIT; hard rule: Apply / Alt / Reject / Override; OQ: the 4-slot shape) each with its one-line keterangan. Long-form context (the sections below) stays available as a pointer, never inlined above the options. Every DEFER-class halt does NOT get this screen — it is quarantined (`write-unit-quarantine.sh`) and answered once in the final report.

Canonical prompt for AI fix proposer subagent dispatched when bolt halts with eligible halt type. User reviews proposed fix + approves/rejects via AskUserQuestion.

**Eligible halt types** (per spec §6.3):
- `test_fail` (after default 3 retries)
- `hard_rule_violated` (with framework pack provenance evidence)
- `pbt_property_violated` (counterexample preserved)

**NOT eligible** (always pure pause; never propose fix):
- `oq_business_p1_unresolved` (needs human business decision)
- `dedup_ambiguous` (needs human judgment)
- `quality_gate_failed` (broader investigation needed)
- `constitution_drift_detected` (audit-significant)
- `bolt_repeated_partial_failure` (structural problem)
- `provenance_missing` (post-flight detected; user must add trailer)

## Contents

- Subagent dispatch contract
- Prompt template
- Main thread post-processing
- Confidence-driven defaults
- Halt cycle safety
- Anti-halu rails
- Performance
- Backward compatibility

## Subagent dispatch contract

execute-bolts post-flight detects halt → if halt type eligible → dispatch fix-proposer subagent with this template → render result via AskUserQuestion → on user-accept apply fix + re-execute bolt → on user-reject continue chain pause.

## Prompt template

```
ROLE: AI fix proposer for mega-sdd bolt halt.

CONTEXT:
- Bolt halt type: <halt_type>
- Unit: <unit_id> "<title>"
- Scope: <scope_id>
- Halt details (verbatim from halt YAML):
  <verbatim halt YAML block>

EVIDENCE FILES (read these via Read tool):
- Unit body: <vault>/units/U-XXX.md
- Bolt report: <vault>/bolts/U-XXX/bolt-report.md (includes bolt's self-assessment + retry history)
- Preflight snapshot: <vault>/bolts/U-XXX/preflight.json
- Postflight snapshot: <vault>/bolts/U-XXX/postflight.json (if any)
- Halt-type-specific evidence:
