134	══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
135	✓ execute-bolts batch complete: 18/20 done, 2 halted, 1 auto-resolved
136	══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
137	  Scope: BE | Duration: 24m11s | Retries: 3 total | Avg confidence: 0.87
138	  Halts open: U-012 (test_fail awaiting user), U-015 (hard_rule_violated)
139	  See <vault>/bolts/_summary.md for the full table
140	  Next: detect-drift (auto-gate, hybrid mode — DEFAULT-ON)
141	```
142	
143	## Aggregate `_summary.md`
144	
145	Auto-generated AFTER every batch (overwrite-safe; idempotent regen) at `<vault>/bolts/_summary.md`:
146	
147	```markdown
148	# Bolts Summary — <Project Name>
149	**Generated**: <ISO8601> (mega-sdd execute-bolts)
150	**Scope**: <scope_id> (<scope_name>)
151	**Batch**: <--all | --squad=X | --module=Y>
152	**Duration**: <duration>
153	**Avg AI confidence**: <0.0-1.0>
154	
155	## Status table
156	| Unit | Title | Status | Duration | Retries | Confidence | Halt type | Commit |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| U-001 | <title> | ✓ done | 45s | 0 | 0.95 | — | <sha> |
159	| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
160	
161	## Halts open (N)
162	- U-XXX: <halt_type> after <retries> retries. <fix proposal status>. Resume: `/mega-sdd --resume`.
163	
164	## Hard rule violations across batch (by rule)
165	| Rule | Source | Violations | Resolution |
166	|---|---|---|---|
167	
168	## Mutability tier coverage (when scope-tagged vault)
169	| Tier | Units touched | Status |
170	|---|---|---|
171	
172	## Self-assessment summary (uncertain decisions across batch)
173	- U-XXX: "<decision>" — fallback: <safer alternative>
174	
175	## Deferred open questions (N)
176	<P3/A6 re-surface — a pure read of vault.json open_questions[] where
177	status == deferred: one line per OQ (tag, priority, reason, defer_to);
178	close with the re-run command `resolve-oq`. N=0 -> omit the
179	section. A defer that never resurfaces is a silent assumption — this
180	section and the chain summary are the resurface.>
181	
182	## Next steps
183	- Resolve <N> halts: `/mega-sdd --resume`
184	- After all green: detect-drift will auto-run (hybrid gate; --no-drift-check opt-out)
185	```
186	
187	Written immediately after the batch loop completes (whether all bolts succeeded, some halted, or the chain was cancelled). Overwrites any prior `_summary.md` (full regen each batch). The `--force-skip-postflight` anti-bypass policy surfaces here when used.
188	
189	## Batch completion — full-suite gate (B2)
190	
191	The per-bolt acceptance command is **scoped** to that unit; nothing re-runs the *whole* project suite. A later bolt — or an out-of-band edit that bypassed the bolt flow — can silently break an earlier bolt's contract and the batch still reports `completed`. The batch-completion gate closes that hole. It applies to EVERY invocation that committed code — a single bolt too, not only batches (relocated here from the batch ref in v7 R4). Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-batch-suite-gate-and-bypass-guard.md`.
192	
193	**When:** once, after the **last committed code-bearing bolt** of the invocation (single bolt or `--all`/`--parallel`/`--per-squad`/`--module` batch). Skipped only for `--dry-run`, a zero-code-commit run (verify-only / all-skipped), or `--no-full-suite` (logged, never silent).
194	
195	**Run the FULL suite, unscoped.** Use the test runner detected at pre-flight check 3.5 with **no per-unit filter** — e.g. `yarn test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...` / `cargo test`, NOT `yarn test <one-file>`. Capture pass/fail/todo counts.
196	
197	**Out-of-band bypass guard (before the verdict).** Record the invocation's base SHA at batch start. Scan `git log <base>..HEAD` **excluding this run's own bolt commits**; for each commit, `git show --name-only` and flag any that touched a file listed in some unit's `target_files` yet whose message carries no `SDD-PROVENANCE` trailer. List them in `bypass_commits[]`. Bounding to the batch window is mandatory — an unscoped scan flags every pre-SDD commit in history. A non-empty list does not by itself halt (the full-suite run is the real gate) but forces the suite to run even on an otherwise-skippable invocation, and is surfaced in `_summary.md`.
198	
199	**Record `<vault>/bolts/_batch-suite.json` — via the sanctioned writer ONLY:** run `bash <plugin>/scripts/run-full-suite.sh --cwd=<project-root>`. The artifact is hook-guarded (a hand-written or agent-written file is denied and would be overwritten anyway); the wrapper runs the suite itself, refuses a dirty code tree, pins the 40-hex HEAD captured BEFORE the run, writes to every discoverable vault, and stamps:
200	
201	```json
202	{ "status": "green|red", "head_sha": "<40-hex sha>", "ran_at": "<iso8601>",
203	  "runner": "<command>", "exit_code": 0, "output_tail": "…",
204	  "written_by": "run-full-suite.sh" }
205	```
206	
207	**Verdict.** `status: red` → **halt `batch_suite_red`**: emit the blocker with the failing test names, leave the tree for review (do not auto-revert), do not emit a `status: completed` handoff. `status: green` → the batch is complete.
208	
209	**Enforcement (the gate is real, not prose).** The Stop hook AND the execute-bolts gate itself run `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --batch-suite-gate` (detection at turn end, turn-gated + re-derivation at gate time). The PreToolUse aggregator blocks the **next** `execute-bolts` when no green `_batch-suite.json` covers the newest **code commit** (`batch_suite_gate_missing` — missing or stale: a code change landed after the last full-suite run, decided via `git merge-base --is-ancestor <newest-code-commit> <gate.head_sha>`; a symbolic `head_sha` like `"HEAD"` is REJECTED — the artifact must pin the 40-hex sha) or the recorded suite is RED (`batch_suite_red` — a red blocks only while it COVERS the newest code commit; a stale red is recorded as `stale_reds` and superseded by fresh evidence). The artifact is written ONLY by `scripts/run-full-suite.sh` (hook-guarded; the wrapper runs the suite and pins HEAD itself). The hook **verifies the artifact; it never runs the suite** (200s+ suites in a hook would cripple every turn). The freshness anchor is the newest commit touching a **code file** (outside `.mega-sdd/` and the legacy vault trees, excluding pure-docs `.md`/`.rst`) **regardless of subject** — so an out-of-band edit (a hotfix, a manual change, a `git pull`) that touches source after a green suite DOES trip the gate (`out_of_band: true`); a docs/markdown-only commit does not. The gate *activates* only once a code-bearing bolt commit exists — recognized by the canonical identity (`<type>(U-XXX):` scope, legacy `(bolt): U-XXX` subject, or `Unit:` trailer; `bolt-contract.md §Commit message format`). No bolting yet ⇒ nothing to gate.
210	
211	**Sync lane.** After `orchestrate-flow --sync` reconciles an out-of-band edit, it COMMITS the reconciliation, then runs `run-full-suite.sh` (the wrapper refuses a dirty code tree — the artifact certifies a commit) — this is the catch for the *post*-batch out-of-band edit the within-batch gate has already passed. (The `SYNC-REPORT.md` terminal emission is owned separately by the sync-report work; it *consumes* this artifact, it does not re-run the suite.)
212	
213	## Outputs detail
214	
215	Per unit:
216	- Code commits (1+) on the current branch (skipped for `task_type: verify` if no changes).
217	- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/bolt-report.md` — frontmatter MUST include `target_hashes:` (living-vault staleness anchor; spec `2026-06-10-living-vault-continuous-sync-design.md` S6):
218	  ```yaml
219	  target_hashes:                       # sha256 of each target_files entry AT COMMIT TIME
220	    <repo-relative-path>: <sha256-hex> # computed by the controller AFTER the commit, from the committed content
221	  ```
222	  `scripts/compute-unit-staleness.sh` later compares these to the working tree — a mismatch marks the unit `stale` for the sync lane. Older bolt-reports without the field → staleness is `unknown` (treated as not-stale; never guessed).
223	- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/preflight.json` — Hard rule pre-flight snapshot for audit + diff (script-written by `run-preflight-scan.sh`; hook-guarded).
224	- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/postflight.json` — Hard rule post-flight check results (per-rule pass/fail + evidence).
225	- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/findings.json` — the review-panel finding ledger (controller-written working state; `review-panel.md §Attempt rounds`).
226	
227	**Evidence-commit batching (spec D7).** When the project versions `.mega-sdd/` in git: ALL state-file refreshes + bolt artifacts produced by one unit's attempt cycle are staged into ONE evidence commit at unit completion (`chore(sdd): evidence U-XXX — …`). A standalone gate-state-refresh commit (`chore(sdd): refresh gate state`) is never emitted — the measured field run landed such commits seconds apart, pure history spam. Projects that gitignore `.mega-sdd/` are unaffected; the unit's CODE commit stays atomic and separate per the bolt contract.
228	
229	Global:
230	- Update `<vault>/vault.json` changelog: `{ "event": "bolt_completed", "unit": "U-XXX", "commits": [...] }`.
231	
232	**Scope traceability:** when `vault.json` has a `scope` field, `bolt-report.md` MUST include scope in its header for multi-squad traceability (read vault.json once at skill start; propagate into the header — NO behavior change to bolt execution):
233	
234	```yaml
235	---
236	unit: U-001
237	scope: <vault.scope_metadata.id>           # omit when the vault has no scope
238	scope_name: <vault.scope_metadata.name>
239	# ... existing fields
240	---
241	```
242	
243	The handoff YAML may include a `scope:` block per `orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md` when the vault has scope.
244	
245	## Hand-off + end-of-chain phasing
246	
247	After the last unit: suggest `detect-drift` to verify all bolts honored the vault; show a summary (N units done, M failed, P skipped).
248	
249	**End-of-chain phase context.** After the final bolt completes successfully (status==completed AND blockers==[]), inspect `vault.json` for `phase` + `phase_total`.
250	
251	**Single source of truth.** BOTH branches below MUST match §Handoff emission (`--auto`) `next_action` (the `next_action:` block of the handoff template below) and the contract's execute-bolts routing row (`orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md §Per-skill expected emissions`): `suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift`. detect-drift is the DEFAULT-ON auto-gate that runs after every execute-bolts batch (`orchestrate-flow/references/chain-execution.md §Hybrid drift gate phase`), so **execute-bolts is never terminal** — the canonical hop is always detect-drift. Phase status is carried as an informational `next_action.hint` (per `chain-execution.md §Phase context` — "This complements the execute-bolts handoff `next_action.hint`"), **never** as `suggested_skill`: advancing to the next KB-rebuild phase is a MANUAL user checkpoint (`generate-intent/references/generation-guide.md §To start the next phase`; `chain-execution.md §Phase context`), NOT an auto-route. Emitting the phase advance as a `suggested_skill` would let the orchestrator consumption loop pass `suggested_args` straight through and auto-cross into the next phase, bypassing that checkpoint.
252	
253	IF `vault.phase < vault.phase_total`:
254	```yaml
255	next_action:
256	  suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
257	  suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the vault has scope_metadata (mirror §Handoff emission `suggested_args` + the contract execute-bolts routing row)
258	  rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
259	  hint: "Phase <N> of <M> complete. To start Phase <N+1> (MANUAL checkpoint — not auto-routed): generate-intent --kb=<KB-path-from-vault.json.kb_source> --phase=<N+1>. Plan: .mega-sdd/knowledge-base/99-rebuild-architecture/suggested-phasing.md §Phase <N+1>."
260	```
261	
262	IF `vault.phase == vault.phase_total` (final phase) OR `phase_total == 1`:
263	```yaml
264	next_action:
265	  suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
266	  suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the vault has scope_metadata
267	  rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
268	  hint: "Phase <N> of <M> complete — all phases finished."
269	```
270	
271	IF `phase` is absent (older vault): default to `phase: 1, phase_total: 1` → use the final-phase (all-finished hint) form above.
272	
273	## Handoff emission (`--auto`)
274	
275	When invoked with `--auto` (typically by `orchestrate-flow --deep` or `/mega-sdd`), emit a handoff YAML at the end of skill output per the local template below — the OPERATIVE spec (`orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md` owns only the base schema + routing index):
276	
277	```yaml
278	handoff:
279	  emitted_by: execute-bolts
280	  emitted_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>
281	  status: completed | halted
282	  notes:
283	    postflight_skipped: <true|false>     # true ONLY when --force-skip-postflight was used this run (anti-bypass audit trail)
284	  artifacts:                             # ONE LINE per bolt dir actually written; NO range shorthand of ANY kind; NO "(N units)" annotations
285	    - <absolute path to vault/bolts/U-001/>
286	    - <absolute path to vault/bolts/U-002/>
287	    # WRONG (range shorthand — DON'T): ellipsis "...", "through", "to", "thru", Unicode "…", or "(16 units)".
288	    # CORRECT: list EACH executed unit on its own line with an absolute path.
289	    # validate-handoff-yaml.sh os.path.exists() each entry.
290	  starterkit_context:                    # passthrough + metrics
291	    reused: false
292	    framework: laravel
293	    auth_lib: sanctum
294	    authz_lib: spatie/permission
295	    ui_stack: "alpine + tailwind + sweetalert2"
296	    libs_count: 47
297	    bolts_used_starterkit_slice: 11
298	    slice_avg_size_kb: 1.6
299	  next_action:
300	    suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
301	    suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the `scope:` block below is present (AUDIT L9): propagate THIS batch's scope so the chained detect-drift inherits it instead of full-scanning. Stays [] for a single-scope vault.
302	    rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
303	  blockers: []   # populated on test_fail / hard_rule_violated / hard_rule_unparseable / hard_rule_unanchored / cross_squad_interface_draft / verify_unit_writable
304	  metrics:
305	    items_processed: <N units ACTUALLY executed/committed — MUST be 0 for a --dry-run/preview or an "all units already done" no-op re-run; never the would-process count. The bolt_artifacts_missing gate keys off this field.>
306	    items_blocked: <N halts encountered>
307	    bolts_used_starterkit_slice: <int>
308	    slice_avg_size_kb: <float>
309	    acceptance_test_concerns:            # harvested from bolt-report.md self-assessment per §Post-flight acceptance-test concern harvest
310	      - unit: U-007
311	        concern: "Test asserts user.id present but doesn't validate id is unique across concurrent requests; implementation may regress under load."
312	      # ... one entry per bolt that flagged a concern; empty array if none
313	  scope:                                 # when the vault has scope_metadata
314	    id: <scope id, e.g., "BE">
315	    name: <scope name>
316	    sibling_scopes: []
317	    prd_sha256: <sha256 from vault.json>
318	```
319	
320	> **Scope propagation to detect-drift (AUDIT L9).** When this handoff carries a `scope:` block, `next_action.suggested_args` MUST include `--scope=<scope.id>` — `detect-drift` accepts `--scope`, and the orchestrator's consumption loop passes `suggested_args` straight through. Deterministically enforced: the gate-time handoff validator (PreToolUse Branch 1a → `validate-handoff-yaml.sh`) FAILs `scope_args_missing` when a scoped execute-bolts handoff routes to detect-drift without `--scope=` in `suggested_args`. Without it, a scope-filtered bolt batch hands off to a **full-scan** drift check (the seam asymmetry: detect-drift propagates scope to ITS downstream, but nothing seeded scope into detect-drift). For a single-scope vault there is no `scope:` block and `suggested_args` stays `[]`.
321	
322	Status `halted` on any entry of the CANONICAL bolt-halt enum (single owner — `handoff-contract.md`'s routing index carries NO copy, only a pointer here, and `halt-taxonomy.md` classifies every entry into always-stop / cycle-eligible / soft; on conflict this list wins):
323	
324	`test_fail` · `hard_rule_violated` · `hard_rule_unparseable` · `hard_rule_unanchored` · `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` · `verify_unit_writable` · `cross_squad_interface_draft` · `module_blocked_by` · `sprint_blocked_by` · `acceptance_path_unowned` · `dep_missing` · `secret_in_code` · `sast_critical_finding` · `dep_not_found` · `review_critical_unresolved` · `pbt_citation_invalid` · `pbt_property_violated` · `batch_suite_red` · `batch_suite_gate_missing` · `postflight_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_red` · `build_broken` · `anchor_missing` · `whitelist_violation` · `commit_rejected_by_hook` · `bolt_repeated_partial_failure` · `partial_state_corrupt` · `dispatch_prompt_too_large` · `bolt_introduces_locked_drift` · `scope_creep_detected` · `provenance_missing` · `self_assessment_missing` · `bolt_artifacts_missing` · `memory_in_use` · `panel_evidence_missing` · `l0_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_expects_missing`
325	
326	Required ONLY under `--auto`.
327	
328	## Bolt-outcomes state (pipeline)
329	
330	`<vault>/.memory/bolt-outcomes.json` is PIPELINE STATE, not the removed learning lane: `query-graph.sh --modules` derives per-unit completion for the module/DoD rollup from it (latest entry per unit wins), and the analyze cross-unit checks read it for context. The controller appends one entry per bolt outcome:
331	
332	- After a bolt completes: `{unit_id, run_at, task_type, status: "completed", duration_ms}`.
333	- After a bolt halts: `{unit_id, run_at, task_type, status: "halted_<type>", halt_reason}`.
334	
335	Append-only JSON (`{"bolts": [...]}`); a later successful re-run simply appends — consumers take the latest entry per unit. Write it directly (small python/Bash append at the Step-0 artifact layer; v7.3.0 removed the memory-write helper — this file stayed because SCRIPTS read it). The v6-era learning fields (`failure_reflection`, concern thresholds, Reflexion reads) are REMOVED with the memory lane; do not write them.

# execute-bolts — Halts, streaming + handoff

Everything downstream of the per-unit gates: the halt protocol (blocker envelope), compact streaming + the aggregate `_summary.md`, outputs detail, and the handoff YAML + the canonical bolt-halt enum + end-of-chain phasing. The full halt YAML bodies, propose-and-confirm UX, the new-halt-types table, and the PBT violation flow live in `halt-recovery.md` (routed from SKILL.md; loaded only when a halt fires or a `properties:` unit is batched).

## Contents
- Halt protocol
- Self-assessment requirement
- Post-flight acceptance-test concern harvest
- Provenance trailer enforcement
- Per-bolt drift check
- Compact streaming progress
- Aggregate `_summary.md`
- Batch completion — full-suite gate (B2)
- Outputs detail
- Hand-off + end-of-chain phasing
- Handoff emission (`--auto`) — incl. the canonical bolt-halt enum
- Bolt-outcomes state (pipeline)

## Halt protocol

Per the bolt-contract failure modes (the bolt-contract ref listed in SKILL.md). BEFORE the envelope YAML, render the keterangan block per `plugins/mega-sdd/references/halt-protocol.md §Consumer dispatch` step 0 — resolve the cause/unit to actual text (which Hard rule, which test, quoted), one line of why the bolt stopped, and gloss each `next_action` code with its consequence (this applies on STANDALONE `execute-bolts` runs too, not only under the orchestrator). Then emit the blocker YAML:

```yaml
blocker:
  unit: U-XXX
  cause: <category>
  details: <verbatim error / test output>
  next_action: <retry | edit unit | manual fix>
```

The full structured halt YAML bodies (`test_fail`, `review_critical_unresolved`), the propose-and-confirm eligibility table + dispatch contract + config override, the new-halt-types table, and the Property-Based Testing violation flow are in `halt-recovery.md` (routed from SKILL.md) — load it only when a halt actually fires or a batched unit carries a non-empty `properties:` field.

## Self-assessment requirement

Every `bolt-report.md` MUST include a `bolt_self_report` YAML block at the end:

```yaml
bolt_self_report:
  confidence: <0.0-1.0>   # bolt subagent's own confidence in this bolt's correctness
  certain_decisions:
    - "<decision with HIGH confidence + evidence>"
  uncertain_decisions:
    - decision: "<what bolt did>"
      rationale: "<why this path was taken>"
      fallback_if_wrong: "<safer alternative if this turns out wrong>"
  retry_history:
    - attempt: 1
      failure: "<verbatim failure if any>"
      fix: "<what was changed>"
```

If `bolt-report.md` lacks this block → halt `self_assessment_missing` (post-flight verification fails). The aggregate `_summary.md` rolls up `uncertain_decisions` across the batch for post-execution human review.

## Post-flight acceptance-test concern harvest

After `bolt-report.md` is written, scan the `bolt_self_report` block (and adjacent self-assessment text) for an `acceptance_test_concern: <non-empty string>` field (written by the bolt subagent per the dispatch-prompt template, listed in SKILL.md, when the implementation passes the acceptance test but feels under-validated):

1. Parse the bottom-of-file YAML blocks.
2. IF `acceptance_test_concern:` is present AND non-empty:
   - Append to the in-memory aggregate: `{unit_id, concern, source: <bolt-report.md path>}`.
   - Log a one-line chat warning: `"⚠ U-XXX flagged acceptance_test_concern: <truncated 100 chars>"`.
3. After all bolts complete (`--all`), assemble the aggregate into handoff `metrics.acceptance_test_concerns: [{unit, concern}]`.
4. Also surfaced via `_summary.md` (a new "## Acceptance-test concerns" sub-section).

No new halt type — concerns are warnings, not blockers. The re-validation path is `generate-units --regenerate --adversarial-subagent --units=<list>` to author stronger acceptance tests, then re-run the affected bolts. orchestrate-flow Step 7's final summary surfaces the count + unit list when non-empty.

## Provenance trailer enforcement

The post-flight scan also verifies every modified file has a provenance trailer comment:

```
Generated by mega-sdd execute-bolts <version>
Unit: U-XXX (vault sha256: <hash>)
Implements claim: C-NNN "<claim text>"
Anchors consulted: <list>
Hard Rules active: <the rule TEXT verbatim, one entry per rule — NOT ids>
```

> `Hard Rules active:` carries the rule TEXT, not ids — unit `## Hard rules` have none, and minting them would fork from `_lib/postflight_rules.py`, the identity model the B1 gate matches against (`context-enrichment.md §Re-decided amendments`, row 2). The dispatch's `Provenance values` block is the implementer's only sanctioned source and hands it text. This scan verifies trailer PRESENCE only, so an id here lands as a malformed-but-present trailer no gate catches.

Language-appropriate comment style (e.g. `//` for JS/PHP/Java, `#` for Python/Ruby, `--` for SQL). Missing trailer → halt `provenance_missing`.

## Per-bolt drift check

After post-flight Hard Rule validation passes (or a proposed-and-confirmed fix is applied), AND BEFORE the unit is accepted as done (the implementer's commit has already landed — detect-after topology per SKILL.md), run a quick scope-filtered drift scan vs the vault. This runs for EVERY implement unit — single run or batch (relocated here from the batch ref in v7 R4; it was never batch-only):

a. Read `vault.json` scope (if a multi-scope vault) OR skip the scope filter.
b. For each file in the unit's `target_files` modified this bolt:
   - Compare current state vs the vault's expected state (from `binding.md` anchors when present).
   - Detect name drift, type drift, behavior drift (per detect-drift categories).
c. If drift is detected on a LOCKED entity (per `data-mutation-policy.md`) → halt `bolt_introduces_locked_drift` (pure-pause; override-only — never propose-and-confirm).
d. If drift is detected on an INTENT/ARTIFACT entity → log to `bolt-report.md` `## Drift introduced` + continue (will surface at the batch-end detect-drift gate).
e. If no drift → log "✓ Drift check: clean" to `bolt-report.md`.

Compact streaming reflects this:

```
└─ Post-flight: Hard Rules ✓ | PBT ✓ | Drift check: clean ✓
```

OR (drift detected):

```
└─ Post-flight: Hard Rules ✓ | PBT ✓ | ⚠️ Drift: order.amount type changed (LOCKED — will halt at gate)
```

## Compact streaming progress

Per-bolt status is TWO lines (M-05 — the old 7-line ▶/└─ block duplicated `_summary.md`, which persists the same detail to disk; ~2.2K tok saved on a 20-bolt batch):

```
▶ Bolt 7/20: U-007 "Create User model" (scope: BE)
✓ Bolt 7/20: U-007 → done in 1m23s, 0 retries, confidence 0.92, anchors 3/3 ✓, commit 8a3f2e1
```

Intermediate stage detail (context load, pre-flight, TDD phases, post-flight verdicts) goes to `_summary.md` only — print it in chat ONLY when a stage fails (the failing stage's line + the halt).

> **"anchors N/N" honesty:** print that count ONLY after actually probing each
> `## Anchors` path at prompt-assembly time — **path exists + the line is within the file,
> and nothing more.** (The older "when the binding recorded an excerpt/sha, the region still
> matches" clause is KEPT DELETED per `context-enrichment.md §Re-decided amendments` row 4:
> no binding-schema field records an excerpt or a sha, and `check-anchor-freshness.sh` — the
> deterministic owner of this question — probes path + line-range only, for the same reason.
> The residual gap is real, which is why the emitted line must state what was probed:
> `Anchors verified N/M (path + line-range only — content drift NOT checked)`.)
> A stale anchor is NOT a halt — inject
> `ANCHOR STALE (verify before use)` in place of its confidence label in the dispatch
> prompt and print `anchors N-1/N ✓, 1 stale` in the done line. Never print a verified
> count no check produced.

Written immediately after the batch loop completes (whether all bolts succeeded, some halted, or the chain was cancelled). Overwrites any prior `_summary.md` (full regen each batch). The `--force-skip-postflight` anti-bypass policy surfaces here when used.

## Batch completion — full-suite gate (B2)

The per-bolt acceptance command is **scoped** to that unit; nothing re-runs the *whole* project suite. A later bolt — or an out-of-band edit that bypassed the bolt flow — can silently break an earlier bolt's contract and the batch still reports `completed`. The batch-completion gate closes that hole. It applies to EVERY invocation that committed code — a single bolt too, not only batches (relocated here from the batch ref in v7 R4). Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-batch-suite-gate-and-bypass-guard.md`.

**When:** once, after the **last committed code-bearing bolt** of the invocation (single bolt or `--all`/`--parallel`/`--per-squad`/`--module` batch). Skipped only for `--dry-run`, a zero-code-commit run (verify-only / all-skipped), or `--no-full-suite` (logged, never silent).

**Run the FULL suite, unscoped.** Use the test runner detected at pre-flight check 3.5 with **no per-unit filter** — e.g. `yarn test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...` / `cargo test`, NOT `yarn test <one-file>`. Capture pass/fail/todo counts.

**Out-of-band bypass guard (before the verdict).** Record the invocation's base SHA at batch start. Scan `git log <base>..HEAD` **excluding this run's own bolt commits**; for each commit, `git show --name-only` and flag any that touched a file listed in some unit's `target_files` yet whose message carries no `SDD-PROVENANCE` trailer. List them in `bypass_commits[]`. Bounding to the batch window is mandatory — an unscoped scan flags every pre-SDD commit in history. A non-empty list does not by itself halt (the full-suite run is the real gate) but forces the suite to run even on an otherwise-skippable invocation, and is surfaced in `_summary.md`.

**Record `<vault>/bolts/_batch-suite.json` — via the sanctioned writer ONLY:** run `bash <plugin>/scripts/run-full-suite.sh --cwd=<project-root>`. The artifact is hook-guarded (a hand-written or agent-written file is denied and would be overwritten anyway); the wrapper runs the suite itself, refuses a dirty code tree, pins the 40-hex HEAD captured BEFORE the run, writes to every discoverable vault, and stamps:

```json
{ "status": "green|red", "head_sha": "<40-hex sha>", "ran_at": "<iso8601>",
  "runner": "<command>", "exit_code": 0, "output_tail": "…",
  "written_by": "run-full-suite.sh" }
```

**Verdict.** `status: red` → **halt `batch_suite_red`**: emit the blocker with the failing test names, leave the tree for review (do not auto-revert), do not emit a `status: completed` handoff. `status: green` → the batch is complete.

**Enforcement (the gate is real, not prose).** The Stop hook AND the execute-bolts gate itself run `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --batch-suite-gate` (detection at turn end, turn-gated + re-derivation at gate time). The PreToolUse aggregator blocks the **next** `execute-bolts` when no green `_batch-suite.json` covers the newest **code commit** (`batch_suite_gate_missing` — missing or stale: a code change landed after the last full-suite run, decided via `git merge-base --is-ancestor <newest-code-commit> <gate.head_sha>`; a symbolic `head_sha` like `"HEAD"` is REJECTED — the artifact must pin the 40-hex sha) or the recorded suite is RED (`batch_suite_red` — a red blocks only while it COVERS the newest code commit; a stale red is recorded as `stale_reds` and superseded by fresh evidence). The artifact is written ONLY by `scripts/run-full-suite.sh` (hook-guarded; the wrapper runs the suite and pins HEAD itself). The hook **verifies the artifact; it never runs the suite** (200s+ suites in a hook would cripple every turn). The freshness anchor is the newest commit touching a **code file** (outside `.mega-sdd/` and the legacy vault trees, excluding pure-docs `.md`/`.rst`) **regardless of subject** — so an out-of-band edit (a hotfix, a manual change, a `git pull`) that touches source after a green suite DOES trip the gate (`out_of_band: true`); a docs/markdown-only commit does not. The gate *activates* only once a code-bearing bolt commit exists — recognized by the canonical identity (`<type>(U-XXX):` scope, legacy `(bolt): U-XXX` subject, or `Unit:` trailer; `bolt-contract.md §Commit message format`). No bolting yet ⇒ nothing to gate.

**Sync lane.** After `orchestrate-flow --sync` reconciles an out-of-band edit, it COMMITS the reconciliation, then runs `run-full-suite.sh` (the wrapper refuses a dirty code tree — the artifact certifies a commit) — this is the catch for the *post*-batch out-of-band edit the within-batch gate has already passed. (The `SYNC-REPORT.md` terminal emission is owned separately by the sync-report work; it *consumes* this artifact, it does not re-run the suite.)

## Outputs detail

Per unit:
- Code commits (1+) on the current branch (skipped for `task_type: verify` if no changes).
- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/bolt-report.md` — frontmatter MUST include `target_hashes:` (living-vault staleness anchor; spec `2026-06-10-living-vault-continuous-sync-design.md` S6):
  ```yaml
  target_hashes:                       # sha256 of each target_files entry AT COMMIT TIME
    <repo-relative-path>: <sha256-hex> # computed by the controller AFTER the commit, from the committed content
  ```
  `scripts/compute-unit-staleness.sh` later compares these to the working tree — a mismatch marks the unit `stale` for the sync lane. Older bolt-reports without the field → staleness is `unknown` (treated as not-stale; never guessed).
- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/preflight.json` — Hard rule pre-flight snapshot for audit + diff (script-written by `run-preflight-scan.sh`; hook-guarded).
- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/postflight.json` — Hard rule post-flight check results (per-rule pass/fail + evidence).
- `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/findings.json` — the review-panel finding ledger (controller-written working state; `review-panel.md §Attempt rounds`).

**Evidence-commit batching (spec D7).** When the project versions `.mega-sdd/` in git: ALL state-file refreshes + bolt artifacts produced by one unit's attempt cycle are staged into ONE evidence commit at unit completion (`chore(sdd): evidence U-XXX — …`). A standalone gate-state-refresh commit (`chore(sdd): refresh gate state`) is never emitted — the measured field run landed such commits seconds apart, pure history spam. Projects that gitignore `.mega-sdd/` are unaffected; the unit's CODE commit stays atomic and separate per the bolt contract.

Global:
- Update `<vault>/vault.json` changelog: `{ "event": "bolt_completed", "unit": "U-XXX", "commits": [...] }`.

**Scope traceability:** when `vault.json` has a `scope` field, `bolt-report.md` MUST include scope in its header for multi-squad traceability (read vault.json once at skill start; propagate into the header — NO behavior change to bolt execution):

```yaml
---
unit: U-001
scope: <vault.scope_metadata.id>           # omit when the vault has no scope
scope_name: <vault.scope_metadata.name>
# ... existing fields
---
```

The handoff YAML may include a `scope:` block per `orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md` when the vault has scope.

## Hand-off + end-of-chain phasing

After the last unit: suggest `detect-drift` to verify all bolts honored the vault; show a summary (N units done, M failed, P skipped).

**End-of-chain phase context.** After the final bolt completes successfully (status==completed AND blockers==[]), inspect `vault.json` for `phase` + `phase_total`.

**Single source of truth.** BOTH branches below MUST match §Handoff emission (`--auto`) `next_action` (the `next_action:` block of the handoff template below) and the contract's execute-bolts routing row (`orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md §Per-skill expected emissions`): `suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift`. detect-drift is the DEFAULT-ON auto-gate that runs after every execute-bolts batch (`orchestrate-flow/references/chain-execution.md §Hybrid drift gate phase`), so **execute-bolts is never terminal** — the canonical hop is always detect-drift. Phase status is carried as an informational `next_action.hint` (per `chain-execution.md §Phase context` — "This complements the execute-bolts handoff `next_action.hint`"), **never** as `suggested_skill`: advancing to the next KB-rebuild phase is a MANUAL user checkpoint (`generate-intent/references/generation-guide.md §To start the next phase`; `chain-execution.md §Phase context`), NOT an auto-route. Emitting the phase advance as a `suggested_skill` would let the orchestrator consumption loop pass `suggested_args` straight through and auto-cross into the next phase, bypassing that checkpoint.

IF `vault.phase < vault.phase_total`:
```yaml
next_action:
  suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
  suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the vault has scope_metadata (mirror §Handoff emission `suggested_args` + the contract execute-bolts routing row)
  rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
  hint: "Phase <N> of <M> complete. To start Phase <N+1> (MANUAL checkpoint — not auto-routed): generate-intent --kb=<KB-path-from-vault.json.kb_source> --phase=<N+1>. Plan: .mega-sdd/knowledge-base/99-rebuild-architecture/suggested-phasing.md §Phase <N+1>."
```

IF `vault.phase == vault.phase_total` (final phase) OR `phase_total == 1`:
```yaml
next_action:
  suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
  suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the vault has scope_metadata
  rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
  hint: "Phase <N> of <M> complete — all phases finished."
```

IF `phase` is absent (older vault): default to `phase: 1, phase_total: 1` → use the final-phase (all-finished hint) form above.

## Handoff emission (`--auto`)

When invoked with `--auto` (typically by `orchestrate-flow --deep` or `/mega-sdd`), emit a handoff YAML at the end of skill output per the local template below — the OPERATIVE spec (`orchestrate-flow/references/handoff-contract.md` owns only the base schema + routing index):

```yaml
handoff:
  emitted_by: execute-bolts
  emitted_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>
  status: completed | halted
  notes:
    postflight_skipped: <true|false>     # true ONLY when --force-skip-postflight was used this run (anti-bypass audit trail)
  artifacts:                             # ONE LINE per bolt dir actually written; NO range shorthand of ANY kind; NO "(N units)" annotations
    - <absolute path to vault/bolts/U-001/>
    - <absolute path to vault/bolts/U-002/>
    # WRONG (range shorthand — DON'T): ellipsis "...", "through", "to", "thru", Unicode "…", or "(16 units)".
    # CORRECT: list EACH executed unit on its own line with an absolute path.
    # validate-handoff-yaml.sh os.path.exists() each entry.
  starterkit_context:                    # passthrough + metrics
    reused: false
    framework: laravel
    auth_lib: sanctum
    authz_lib: spatie/permission
    ui_stack: "alpine + tailwind + sweetalert2"
    libs_count: 47
    bolts_used_starterkit_slice: 11
    slice_avg_size_kb: 1.6
  next_action:
    suggested_skill: mega-sdd:detect-drift
    suggested_args: []                     # → ["--scope=<id>"] when the `scope:` block below is present (AUDIT L9): propagate THIS batch's scope so the chained detect-drift inherits it instead of full-scanning. Stays [] for a single-scope vault.
    rationale: "All bolts executed; recommend a periodic drift check."
  blockers: []   # populated on test_fail / hard_rule_violated / hard_rule_unparseable / hard_rule_unanchored / cross_squad_interface_draft / verify_unit_writable
  metrics:
    items_processed: <N units ACTUALLY executed/committed — MUST be 0 for a --dry-run/preview or an "all units already done" no-op re-run; never the would-process count. The bolt_artifacts_missing gate keys off this field.>
    items_blocked: <N halts encountered>
    bolts_used_starterkit_slice: <int>
    slice_avg_size_kb: <float>
    acceptance_test_concerns:            # harvested from bolt-report.md self-assessment per §Post-flight acceptance-test concern harvest
      - unit: U-007
        concern: "Test asserts user.id present but doesn't validate id is unique across concurrent requests; implementation may regress under load."
      # ... one entry per bolt that flagged a concern; empty array if none
  scope:                                 # when the vault has scope_metadata
    id: <scope id, e.g., "BE">
    name: <scope name>
    sibling_scopes: []
    prd_sha256: <sha256 from vault.json>
```

> **Scope propagation to detect-drift (AUDIT L9).** When this handoff carries a `scope:` block, `next_action.suggested_args` MUST include `--scope=<scope.id>` — `detect-drift` accepts `--scope`, and the orchestrator's consumption loop passes `suggested_args` straight through. Deterministically enforced: the gate-time handoff validator (PreToolUse Branch 1a → `validate-handoff-yaml.sh`) FAILs `scope_args_missing` when a scoped execute-bolts handoff routes to detect-drift without `--scope=` in `suggested_args`. Without it, a scope-filtered bolt batch hands off to a **full-scan** drift check (the seam asymmetry: detect-drift propagates scope to ITS downstream, but nothing seeded scope into detect-drift). For a single-scope vault there is no `scope:` block and `suggested_args` stays `[]`.

Status `halted` on any entry of the CANONICAL bolt-halt enum (single owner — `handoff-contract.md`'s routing index carries NO copy, only a pointer here, and `halt-taxonomy.md` classifies every entry into always-stop / cycle-eligible / soft; on conflict this list wins):

`test_fail` · `hard_rule_violated` · `hard_rule_unparseable` · `hard_rule_unanchored` · `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` · `verify_unit_writable` · `cross_squad_interface_draft` · `module_blocked_by` · `sprint_blocked_by` · `acceptance_path_unowned` · `dep_missing` · `secret_in_code` · `sast_critical_finding` · `dep_not_found` · `review_critical_unresolved` · `pbt_citation_invalid` · `pbt_property_violated` · `batch_suite_red` · `batch_suite_gate_missing` · `postflight_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_red` · `build_broken` · `anchor_missing` · `whitelist_violation` · `commit_rejected_by_hook` · `bolt_repeated_partial_failure` · `partial_state_corrupt` · `dispatch_prompt_too_large` · `bolt_introduces_locked_drift` · `scope_creep_detected` · `provenance_missing` · `self_assessment_missing` · `bolt_artifacts_missing` · `memory_in_use` · `panel_evidence_missing` · `l0_evidence_missing` · `acceptance_expects_missing`

Required ONLY under `--auto`.

## Bolt-outcomes state (pipeline)

`<vault>/.memory/bolt-outcomes.json` is PIPELINE STATE, not the removed learning lane: `query-graph.sh --modules` derives per-unit completion for the module/DoD rollup from it (latest entry per unit wins), and the analyze cross-unit checks read it for context. The controller appends one entry per bolt outcome:

- After a bolt completes: `{unit_id, run_at, task_type, status: "completed", duration_ms}`.
- After a bolt halts: `{unit_id, run_at, task_type, status: "halted_<type>", halt_reason}`.

Append-only JSON (`{"bolts": [...]}`); a later successful re-run simply appends — consumers take the latest entry per unit. Write it directly (small python/Bash append at the Step-0 artifact layer; v7.3.0 removed the memory-write helper — this file stayed because SCRIPTS read it). The v6-era learning fields (`failure_reflection`, concern thresholds, Reflexion reads) are REMOVED with the memory lane; do not write them.

# Unit U-004 — Bangun halaman Beranda

## Goal

Halaman `/beranda` menampilkan judul organisasi, tagline, tiga layanan dari konfigurasi, dan tombol ke Kontak.

## Context (read first)

Beranda adalah titik masuk alur F-U-002 (flows.md): pengunjung membaca profil singkat lalu bisa menuju Kontak (PRD §Halaman Beranda). Konten dibaca dari `companyProfile` di `src/configs/companyProfile` (dibuat U-001 — unit ini meng-import file itu, karena itu `depends_on: [U-001]`). Halaman berada di route group `(public-pages)` dari OQ-AR-3.

## Anchors

- src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/login/page.tsx:1-22 — pola page App Router: `metadata` + default export yang merender komponen view

## Hard rules

- DO NOT modify package.json

> Sumber: binding.md §Suggested Unit Hard Rules (C-AR-05, C-CN-07).

## Implementation steps

1. Buat `src/features/company-profile/components/BerandaView/index.tsx` yang merender `organizationName` sebagai satu-satunya heading level 1, `tagline`, tiga kartu layanan (judul + paragraf) dari `companyProfile.services`, dan tombol MUI yang merupakan link `next/link` ke `/kontak`; tata letaknya memakai grid/stack MUI yang menumpuk di layar sempit (375px) dan berjajar di desktop.
2. Buat `src/app/(public-pages)/beranda/page.tsx` yang mengekspor `metadata` (title dari `organizationName`) dan merender `BerandaView`.
3. Tulis `index.test.tsx` di folder yang sama memakai `renderWithProviders` dengan empat judul test persis seperti `expects`, dan bandingkan teks yang tampil dengan nilai yang di-import dari `@/configs/companyProfile` (bukan teks yang ditulis ulang di test); link Kontak diperiksa lewat `getByRole('link')` dengan `href` `/kontak`.

## Acceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative).

3	import { getServerSession } from 'next-auth'
4	
5	import { authOptions } from './libs/auth'
6	
7	export async function proxy(request: Request) {
8	  const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)
9	  const { pathname } = new URL(request.url)
10	
11	  const publicRoutes = ['/login', '/register']
12	  const isPublicRoute = publicRoutes.includes(pathname)
13	
14	  if (session?.error === 'RefreshTokenError') {
15	    // Clear the session cookie and redirect — no signOut() needed here
16	    const response = NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
17	
18	    response.cookies.delete('next-auth.session-token')
19	    response.cookies.delete('__Secure-next-auth.session-token') // for HTTPS
20	
21	    return response
22	  }
23	
24	  if (session?.accessToken && isPublicRoute) {
25	    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
26	  }
27	
28	  if (!session?.accessToken && !isPublicRoute) {
29	    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
30	  }
31	
32	  return NextResponse.next()
33	}

19	
20	Judul organisasi, tagline satu kalimat, ringkasan tiga layanan utama (judul + satu paragraf per layanan, konten statis dari file konfigurasi), tombol menuju halaman Kontak. Responsif di 375px dan desktop.
21	
22	## Halaman Tentang Kami
23	
24	Profil singkat (dua–tiga paragraf statis), daftar tim (nama + peran, statis dari konfigurasi, tanpa foto), dan tautan kembali ke Beranda.
25	
26	## Halaman Kontak
27	
28	Form dengan field: nama (wajib, ≤100 karakter), email (wajib, format email valid), pesan (wajib, ≤2000 karakter). Saat dikirim: validasi sisi server, simpan ke tabel `contact_messages`, tampilkan pesan sukses di halaman yang sama. Gagal validasi → tampilkan error per field, isi form tidak hilang.
29	
30	## Data model
31	
32	```dbml
33	Table contact_messages {
34	  id integer [pk]
35	  name varchar(100) [not null]
36	  email varchar(255) [not null]
37	  message text [not null]
38	  created_at timestamp [not null]
39	}
40	```
41	
42	## Alur
43	
44	### F-U-001: Kirim pesan kontak
45	
46	1. Pengunjung membuka Halaman Kontak.
47	2. Mengisi nama, email, pesan → klik Kirim.
48	3. Server memvalidasi tiga field.
49	4. Valid → simpan `contact_messages` → tampilkan "Pesan terkirim".
50	5. Tidak valid → tampilkan error per field, form tetap terisi.
51	
52	**Definition of Done**
53	- [ ] Pesan valid tersimpan dengan `created_at`.
54	- [ ] Email tidak valid ditolak dengan pesan error di field email.
55	- [ ] Form tetap terisi setelah gagal validasi.

63	| Keamanan | Input form di-escape saat ditampilkan; tidak ada HTML mentah dari pengunjung. |

1	import type { Session } from 'next-auth'
2	
3	import type { ApiResponse } from '@/types/common'
4	
5	export type RequestOptions = RequestInit & {
6	  params?: Record<string, string>
7	}
8	
9	type FetcherConfig = {
10	  baseURL: string
11	
12	  /** Browser uses getSession(); server uses getServerSession(authOptions). */
13	  getSession: () => Promise<Session | null>
14	
15	  /**
16	   * How a non-OK response is handled. The browser fetcher throws (so mutation
17	   * hooks surface the message via onError); the server fetcher returns a
18	   * `{ success: false }` envelope. Either way the return type is the envelope.
19	   */
20	  onError: (res: Response) => Promise<ApiResponse<unknown>>
21	}
22	
23	/**
24	 * Shared fetcher core for both apiClient (browser) and apiServer (RSC / route
25	 * handlers). The only differences between them — session source and error
26	 * handling — are injected via config; everything else (header building, URL
27	 * building, the verb wrappers) lives here so the two stay in lockstep.
28	 */
29	export function createFetcher({ baseURL, getSession, onError }: FetcherConfig) {
30	  async function getHeaders(customHeaders?: HeadersInit): Promise<HeadersInit> {
31	    const session = await getSession()
32	
33	    return {
34	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
35	      ...(session?.accessToken && {
36	        Authorization: `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`
37	      }),
38	      ...customHeaders
39	    }
40	  }
41	
42	  function buildURL(path: string, params?: Record<string, string>): string {
43	    // apiClient's baseURL is a same-origin relative prefix ('/api'); resolve it
44	    // against the browser origin. apiServer's baseURL is already absolute, so the
45	    // base is ignored there (and window is undefined on the server anyway).
46	    const base = typeof window === 'undefined' ? undefined : window.location.origin
47	    const url = new URL(`${baseURL}${path}`, base)
48	
49	    if (params) {
50	      Object.entries(params).forEach(([k, v]) => url.searchParams.set(k, v))
51	    }
52	
53	    return url.toString()
54	  }
55	
56	  async function request<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> {
57	    const { params, headers, ...rest } = options
58	
59	    const res = await fetch(buildURL(path, params), {
60	      ...rest,
61	      headers: await getHeaders(headers)
62	    })
63	
64	    if (!res.ok) {
65	      return onError(res) as Promise<ApiResponse<T>>
66	    }
67	
68	    return res.json() as Promise<ApiResponse<T>>
69	  }
70	
71	  return {
72	    get: <T>(path: string, options?: RequestOptions) => request<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'GET' }),
73	    post: <T>(path: string, body: unknown, options?: RequestOptions) =>
74	      request<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
75	    put: <T>(path: string, body: unknown, options?: RequestOptions) =>
76	      request<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
77	    delete: <T>(path: string, options?: RequestOptions) => request<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' })
78	  }
79	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# merge-panel-findings.sh — the SOLE writer of <vault>/bolts/U-XXX/findings.json
# (spec 2026-08-29 Fase 1).
#
# Why this exists. The severity->status mapping in review-panel.md §Attempt
# rounds was PROSE, applied by whatever model was driving the controller. Field
# measurement (HOST-AS400 U-001, panel complete, spec_verdict pass): 2 critical
# + 7 important + 4 minor, and ALL THIRTEEN were stamped `status: open`. The
# contract says Critical and the findings behind a spec-fail enter as `open`;
# Important/Minor enter as `advisory` — recorded, surfaced, NEVER gating. So 11
# of 13 findings (85%) held the fix round hostage: the implementer's fix scope
# and the resolution-verifier's workload both scaled by 6.5x over a naming nit.
# Prose that says "never gating" enforces nothing (gates > rules > hooks).
#
# What it does, deterministically:
#   1. Parse each lens's FINDINGS: block (rows `severity | file:line | title | detail`).
#   2. Evidence-or-drop — a row with no resolvable file:line is DISCARDED and counted.
#   3. Dedup — same (file, +/-3 lines, same title stem) across lenses -> ONE entry at
#      MAX severity, `lenses[]` records every reporter.
#   4. Consensus — reported by >=2 lenses -> confidence: high.
#   5. Status mapping — critical UNION spec-fail-linked -> open; important/minor ->
#      advisory. This is the whole point; it is not a judgment call.
#   6. Stable IDs across rounds — an existing finding keeps its id and its
#      resolution history; a re-reported issue never gets a duplicate new id.
#
# Verifier rounds (--verifier=<file>) consume RESOLUTIONS: + NEW-FINDINGS: and
# apply the same mapping to the new rows; `resolved` REQUIRES new-head evidence
# (a resolution row with no file:line stays open — evidence-gated resolution).
#
# Usage:
#   merge-panel-findings.sh --vault=<dir> --unit=U-XXX --head=<sha> [--round=N]
#       [--spec-verdict=pass|fail] --lens=<name>:<file> [--lens=... ...]
#   merge-panel-findings.sh --vault=<dir> --unit=U-XXX --head=<sha> --round=N
#       --verifier=<file>
#
# Exit: 0 = ledger written (stdout = one-line JSON summary incl. gate verdict)
#       2 = usage error. Never exits non-zero on findings — the GATE reads
#           `open_count` from the summary/ledger; this script records, it does
#           not decide to halt.
set -u
VAULT=""; UNIT=""; HEAD_SHA=""; ROUND=1; SPEC_VERDICT=""; VERIFIER=""
LENSES=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  --vault=*) VAULT="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --unit=*) UNIT="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --head=*) HEAD_SHA="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --round=*) ROUND="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --spec-verdict=*) SPEC_VERDICT="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --verifier=*) VERIFIER="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --lens=*) LENSES="${LENSES}${1#*=}"$'\n'; shift;;

drop={'quality':{'## Context (read first)','## Implementation steps'},

EOF

10	You review whether a mega-sdd bolt's implementation is **safe to ship**. Your task prompt contains the unit body (requirements, Hard rules, binding_refs), the base/head commit SHAs, and optionally a framework-pack security slice and the PATH to the deterministic L0 scan results file (Read it before judging). You run blind: you never see the implementer's report or any other reviewer's verdict — form your judgment from the code alone.
11	
12	## Do not trust anything but the diff
13	
14	Inspect the actual change (`git diff <base>..<head>`) and read every file it touched. Pull surrounding code via Read/Grep when a finding needs context (a missing authz check is only provable by reading the route/middleware chain around it).
15	
16	## What to check — adversarial, in priority order
17	
18	Try to find what is **wrong**; do not grade generously. These are the classes AI-generated code measurably introduces:
19	
20	1. **Missing input validation / injection** — user-controlled data reaching SQL/shell/template/path/deserialization sinks without validation or parameterization (SQLi, command injection, XSS, path traversal).
21	2. **Authn/authz gaps vs the unit spec** — does every new route/action enforce the authentication and authorization the unit, binding, or constitution requires? A handler that *works* but skips the access check is a Critical finding, not a style issue.
22	3. **Secrets** — hard-coded credentials, API keys, tokens, connection strings; secrets written to logs or fixtures.
23	4. **New dependencies** — any dependency this change adds: is it necessary, does it actually exist on the official registry, is it the canonical package name (not a near-miss the model may have hallucinated)? Unvetted or unnecessary new deps are findings.
24	5. **Fail-open error handling** — catch-and-continue around security checks, broad exception swallowing that defaults to access, missing failure paths in auth flows.
25	6. **Architectural drift** — a design change that silently bypasses an existing security control (middleware skipped, validation layer circumvented, scope filter dropped) with no syntax violation. Compare the change against the unit's Anchors and binding_refs.
26	7. **Sensitive-data handling** — PII/credentials in responses, mass-assignment exposure, missing tenant/branch scoping where sibling code applies it.
27	
28	If your prompt names a deterministic scan-results file (SAST/secret-scan), Read it and do NOT re-report those findings — verify they were addressed and look for what the scanners cannot see (items 2 and 6 above are yours alone).
29	
30	## Grade honestly
31	
32	- **Critical** — exploitable or access-control-relevant; must fix before the bolt is accepted — the commit has already landed (detect-after), so remediation is fix-forward or revert (injection, missing authz, secret, fail-open auth, drift bypassing a control).
33	- **Important** — weakens posture; should fix (missing validation on low-exposure input, over-broad exception handling, unpinned risky dep).
34	- **Minor** — hardening opportunity.
35	
36	Every finding gets a `file:line` reference, the vulnerability class, and a concrete fix. A finding you cannot anchor to code does not go in the report. Do not invent problems to look thorough — if the change is clean, say so.

## What was implemented

- `src/libs/public-routes/index.ts` (created) exports `PUBLIC_PAGE_ROUTES = ['/beranda', '/tentang-kami', '/kontak'] as const` and `isPublicPageRoute(pathname)`, which matches only those three exact strings. `/kontakx`, `/kontak/detail` and `/Kontak` do not match.
- `src/proxy.ts` (modified) computes `pathname` first and returns `NextResponse.next()` for `isPublicPageRoute(pathname)` before `getServerSession` runs. All other branches are unchanged: the `publicRoutes` list for `/login` and `/register`, the RefreshTokenError cookie clear and redirect, the bounce of signed-in users to `/home`, the redirect of anonymous visitors to `/login`, and `config.matcher`. The signature `export async function proxy(request: Request)` is unchanged.
- `src/libs/public-routes/index.test.ts` (created) has 7 tests whose titles match the `acceptance_test.expects` strings exactly. The guard tests call `proxy(new Request(...))` with `vi.mock('next-auth')` controlling `getServerSession`, then check the `location` header.

## Tests

- TDD red with the pragma: under `// @vitest-environment node` the suite could not load: `ReferenceError: window is not defined` at `src/test/setup.ts:41:23`.
- TDD red under jsdom (before the `proxy.ts` change): 2 of 7 failed for the expected reason (`expected 'http://localhost:3000/login' to be null`). These were "lets an anonymous visitor open a public page without redirect" and "allows a user with a refresh-token error to view a public page without a login redirect".
- Green: `pnpm test:run src/libs/public-routes --reporter=verbose`: 7/7 passed.

- `eslint` on the three files: no issues. `tsc --noEmit -p .`: no errors in the changed files.

## What was implemented

- `src/features/company-profile/schemas/contact-message/index.ts` — `contactMessageSchema` (`name`: trimmed string, required, max 100; `email`: `z.email`, required; `message`: trimmed string, required, max 2000), `ContactMessageValues` (z.infer), `contactMessageDefaults` (`{ name: '', email: '', message: '' }`), exported `CONTACT_NAME_MAX` / `CONTACT_MESSAGE_MAX`. Error wording is a neutral English placeholder (final copy is still TBD from the PO).
- `src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts` — own `POST(req: NextRequest)` handler (not `proxyPost`): reads JSON (a body that isn't valid JSON is treated as `undefined`, so validation fails), then `safeParse`. On failure it returns `400 { success: false, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: 'Validation failed', data: { errors: z.flattenError(...).fieldErrors } }` without calling upstream. On success it runs `apiServer.post('/v1/contact-messages', parsed.data)` and returns the envelope with status 400 if `success === false`, otherwise 200. This is the same mapping as `respond` in route-handler.ts.

## Tests

Command: `pnpm test:run src/features/company-profile/schemas/contact-message src/app/api/v1/contact-messages --reporter=verbose` — 2 files, 12 tests, all passed. The 9 `expects` titles appear verbatim as test names. TDD red was confirmed first: both suites failed with "Failed to resolve import" before implementation. ESLint is clean on all four files, and `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in them.

Step 3 prescribes `// @vitest-environment node` for route.test.ts. Empirically this cannot run: the shared setup file `src/test/setup.ts:41` calls `Object.defineProperty(window, 'matchMedia', …)` and throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` under the node environment. The failing suite was reproduced before any implementation. setup.ts is outside target_files and is shared by sibling bolts, so I did not modify it. route.test.ts therefore runs in the default jsdom environment. - DO NOT modify src/libs/api/server.ts — untouched (used as-is)
- DO NOT modify src/libs/api/base-fetcher.ts — untouched
- DO NOT modify src/libs/api/route-handler.ts — untouched (its `respond` mapping mirrored, not imported, because it is not exported)

- candidate: `proxyPost` (src/libs/api/route-handler.ts:43) — decision: not_applicable — reason: forwards the raw body without validation; the unit explicitly requires its own handler.
- candidate: `respond` (src/libs/api/route-handler.ts:19) — decision: reimplemented — reason: module-private (not exported) and route-handler.ts is under a DO-NOT-MODIFY hard rule; the one-line status mapping is duplicated inline.
- candidate: `apiServer` (src/libs/api/server.ts:9) — decision: reused.
- candidate: `z.flattenError` (zod 4.3.6) — decision: reused for per-field errors.
- candidate: MSW `server` (src/test/handlers.ts) — decision: reused in route.test.ts via `server.use(...)`.

**Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.** The contact-form validation and the `POST /api/v1/contact-messages` endpoint are built and committed as 57fe6980a98b4c78df94a0ef1af84cfa2d97adf9. One step in the dispatch could not run as written, so I changed it (details below).

**What was built**
- **Validation schema** (`src/features/company-profile/schemas/contact-message/index.ts`): `contactMessageSchema` checks that name is required and at most 100 characters, email is required and valid, and message is required and at most 2000 characters. Name and message are trimmed first, so input that is only spaces is rejected. The file also exports the type `ContactMessageValues` and empty defaults `contactMessageDefaults`. Error messages are neutral English placeholders because the final wording (OQ-FL-1) hasn't been decided.
- **Endpoint** (`src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts`): its own handler, not `proxyPost`, because `proxyPost` forwards the body unvalidated.
  - Invalid input or a body that isn't valid JSON returns 400 with `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` and errors per field, and the upstream API is never called.
  - Valid input is forwarded through `apiServer.post('/v1/contact-messages', …)` with only the trimmed name, email and message. Extra fields like `id`, `created_at` or `isAdmin` are dropped.
  - A failed upstream response comes back as 400; success returns the upstream response unchanged with 200.

**Tests:** the acceptance command passes 12 of 12, and each of the 9 required test names appears word for word. I confirmed both test files failed before the code existed. ESLint is clean on all four files and `tsc --noEmit` shows no errors in them.

**Concern: test environment.** The dispatch says `route.test.ts` should start with `// @vitest-environment node`. That crashes with `ReferenceError: window is not defined`, because the shared `src/test/setup.ts` uses `window` at line 41. That file is outside my allowed files and sibling bolts use it too, so I left it alone. The route test runs in the default jsdom environment instead, where I checked that `NextRequest`/`NextResponse` and the upstream mock behave correctly. The `vi.mock('next-auth')` with no session is kept as prescribed. If the node environment matters, a follow-up can make `setup.ts` skip its `window` setup when `window` is undefined, then add the directive back.

**Hard rules:** none of `package.json`, `src/libs/api/server.ts`, `src/libs/api/base-fetcher.ts` or `src/libs/api/route-handler.ts` changed since the pre-wave head bd66ccb. The commit contains only the four target files, staged by explicit path, with the three required trailers. All four files carry the provenance header, filled from the dispatch's values block.

**reuse_decisions**
- `proxyPost`: not_applicable (it forwards the body without validation; the unit requires its own handler).
- `respond` in `route-handler.ts`: reimplemented as one inline line, because it isn't exported and that file must not be modified.
- `apiServer`: reused.
- zod's `z.flattenError`: reused for the per-field errors.
- The shared MSW test server: reused.
- The `reuse-index.yaml` file doesn't exist (the dispatch records this), so the full index scan wasn't possible; I checked `src/libs/api` and `src/test` directly.

**Other notes**
- The first commit attempt passed all four paths as one string and matched nothing, so nothing was committed; the retry with literal paths worked. At that point HEAD was sibling U-002's commit.
- I couldn't get a final review from the advisor because it was rate-limited.
- The required `bolt-report.md` is written but not committed; the controller reads it from disk.

**Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS**

Anyone can now open `/beranda`, `/tentang-kami` and `/kontak` without logging in, and logged-in users are no longer sent away from them. All 7 acceptance tests pass, and the full suite passes (51 tests). Committed as `91f5a3b8b371bdc07bd28f9626c458c8e1e4d40d`.

**What changed**
- **`src/libs/public-routes/index.ts`** (new): the list of the three pages and `isPublicPageRoute(pathname)`, which only accepts those exact paths. `/kontakx`, `/kontak/detail` and `/Kontak` don't match.
- **`src/proxy.ts`**: the guard lets those three paths through before it looks up the session. Nothing else changed: login/register still send logged-in users to `/home`, a refresh-token error still clears cookies and redirects, other routes still send anonymous visitors to `/login`, and `config.matcher` and the function signature are the same.
- **`src/libs/public-routes/index.test.ts`** (new): 7 tests named exactly as in `acceptance_test`. They run `proxy()` with a mocked session and check the redirect header. Test 1 also checks the session is never looked up for public pages.

**Tests**
- Before changing the guard, 2 of 7 failed for the right reason (`expected 'http://localhost:3000/login' to be null`).
- After: `pnpm test:run src/libs/public-routes --reporter=verbose` passes 7/7, and `pnpm test:run` passes 9 files / 51 tests.
- eslint is clean on all three files, and tsc reports no errors in them.
